You are tasked with summarizing the raw content of a webpage retrieved from a web search. Your goal is to create a summary that preserves the most important information from the original web page. This summary will be used by a downstream research agent, so it's crucial to maintain the key details without losing essential information.

Here is the raw content of the webpage:

<webpage_content>
![](https://braziljournal.com/wp-content/themes/project_theme//assets/img/bj-logo-print.png?x85156)

# [Brazil Journal](https://braziljournal.com)

[Tecnologia](https://braziljournal.com/tecnologia/) 

# Cielo, Stone, Linx e PagSeguro: quem vai liderar?

  

O mercado brasileiro de credenciadoras de cartão terá um novo líder em alguns anos – ou ainda mais cedo, se os atuais líderes não mudarem sua estratégia.

O negócio de credenciamento é uma commodity. Apesar desta afirmação ser óbvia para alguns, a maioria das credenciadoras ainda não percebeu isso e continua a competir apenas com base no preço.

Mas a guerra brutal pelo mercado será vencida por aqueles players que conseguirem atender as necessidades do varejista além de pagamentos. Isso significa entender a cadeia de valor do comerciante, identificar “dores”, criar e ofertar soluções.

Dois grandes grupos de problemas e soluções irão dominar as próximas batalhas dessa guerra pela liderança:

a) Oferta de serviços e soluções financeiras para atacar problemas: as altas taxas de juros, baixa oferta de crédito, fees e despesas bancárias, serviços de cobrança etc;

b) Tecnologia: há um grande espaço para a melhoria dos sistemas de automação, softwares e aplicativos que proporcionem aumento nas vendas, fidelização e melhoria na operação.

Os exemplos acima são apenas algumas das áreas que, uma vez integradas aos meios de pagamento, trarão enormes benefícios para os comerciantes de produtos e serviços no varejo.

Com pouquíssimas exceções, um terminal POS conectado a uma credenciadora é um sistema totalmente apartado, que roda paralelamente a frente de caixa da loja. No final do dia, os comerciantes precisam conciliar suas vendas registradas com o extrato fornecido pela credenciadora e o extrato bancário.

Além disso, a maioria dos sistemas de automação do comerciante é baseada em hardware, o que dificulta a integração, resultando em uma enorme oportunidade para os provedores de tecnologia.

Os terminais POS são coisa do passado.  Quem quiser ser líder em pagamentos tem que pensar em como se livrar dos plásticos e dos terminais. Os pagamentos tornaram-se invisíveis em alguns setores, e serão invisíveis em toda a indústria no futuro.

Quais players podem tomar a liderança? Vejamos o movimento de algumas credenciadoras e seus possíveis impactos na disputa pelo mercado.

**Stone:**

A Stone foi provavelmente a primeira a explorar no Brasil a ideia de integrar tecnologia e meios de pagamento (“software Integration”). Considere todas as empresas que a Stone adicionou aos seus ativos. Eles já podem oferecer serviços adicionais, integrados à solução de pagamento, ajudando os comerciantes a reconciliar suas vendas, integrar pagamentos à frente de caixa, liquidar transações em contas divididas (“split settlement”), serviços financeiros, software de automação, ERP, etc.

Capacidade de distribuição é um fator chave de sucesso. A Stone contratou um exército de vendas e criou o que eles chamam de Stone HUB. A ideia é estar mais perto do comerciante. Um Stone HUB é um pequeno escritório que cobre uma área geográfica com até 400 mil habitantes. Nas grandes cidades, como São Paulo, um HUB abrangerá um bairro, por exemplo.

Isso soa insano devido ao alto custo de aquisição de clientes (o CAC, ou customer acquisition cost), no entanto, à medida que oferta outros produtos além de pagamentos, a Stone pode obter uma redução sensível em seu CAC. Como a Stone não está vinculada a nenhum banco, acredito que essa era sua única saída possível para distribuição e crescimento rápido. Por outro lado, existe um alto risco de insucesso. Uma abordagem de vendas digitais reduziria ainda mais o CAC, mas talvez os comerciantes brasileiros ainda não sejam facilmente alcançáveis ​​por meios digitais.

De qualquer forma, com os HUBs e o exército de vendas, a Stone já está tendo o benefício de um aumento em seu reconhecimento da marca. Oferecer não apenas soluções financeiras, mas também serviços de tecnologia, colocou a Stone na dianteira dessa batalha, diferenciando-a da concorrência.

**PagSeguro:**

A PagSeguro nasceu digital e utiliza os terminais POS móveis para atender um mercado totalmente novo, os chamados microcomerciantes.

Como a grande maioria dos MEIs (microempreendedores individuais) não aceita cartões de crédito ou débito, e como mais de 80% não têm uma conta bancária, os bancos e credenciadoras nunca prestaram atenção nesse segmento.

Ao oferecer a possibilidade de comprar seus próprios terminais mPOS (mobile POS), combinados com uma conta de pagamento, a PagSeguro foi capaz de crescer rapidamente neste segmento com um nível de fidelização jamais visto. Mais de 70% dos clientes da PagSeguro transacionam mensalmente.

Além disso a PagSeguro agora tem seu próprio banco, e aumentará a carteira de serviços financeiros de “conta bancária” para “o que você precisar”. Sua intenção velada é se tornar o banco para microcomerciantes e PMEs.

A PagSeguro nasceu digital, e acredito que em breve lançará produtos diferentes que substituirão a necessidade de um mPOS — talvez, migrando totalmente para pagamentos móveis.

**Os novos players:**

Os IPOs da PagSeguro e Stone abalaram o mercado e acordaram outros players. Se uma instituição financeira e empresas de pagamentos podem adicionar capacidade tecnológica para competir melhor, por que uma gigante de tecnologia não pode oferecer pagamentos e serviços financeiros?

Não estou falando de Google, Facebook, WhatsApp, Amazon, Apple ou Samsung. Sabemos que essas empresas olham para o futuro dos pagamentos e, de certa forma, já atuam nisto principalmente fora do Brasil.

Olhamos os fornecedores de software, empresas que já possuem grande base de clientes, como a Linx. É muito cedo para falar sobre a Linx, mas as duas maiores credenciadoras do mercado perderam a oportunidade de estabelecer uma parceria comercial com essa empresa de tecnologia.

No final de 2018, a Linx lançou a Linx Pay.  Mais do que uma sub credenciadora, a Linx Pay faz parte de uma plataforma que combina diferentes alternativas para atender o cliente. O mercado tem que acompanhar a capacidade de execução da Linx e ver como eles irão impactar o mercado de pagamentos.

**Os atuais líderes:**

Podemos ver a integração de pagamentos com serviços financeiros ofertados por outros players, como Rede, GetNet e SafraPay.

Entretanto, a fórmula que combina “conta bancária + credenciamento + financiamento” — assumindo que não seja uma “venda casada” — é uma oferta relativamente igual entre os concorrentes e, no final do dia, o preço é a única diferenciação.

Depois de ser adquirida pelo Itaú, a Rede passou um bom tempo buscando eficiência e integrando suas áreas com o próprio banco. Como resultado, deve continuar perdendo as parcerias que construiu com outros bancos. Muitos desses resolveram lançar sua própria credenciadora. Sem inovação e integrada ao banco controlador, espera-se que tenha um market share equivalente ao market share do Itaú.

A Cielo teve todo o tempo, dinheiro, pessoas e conhecimento para mudar o mercado, manter sua posição de liderança e ser reconhecida com uma companhia inovadora. Mas até agora, a companhia nada fez de disruptivo. Mesmo o esforço de inovação que foi a LIO vai na contramão do imperativo de mercado: “não gaste dinheiro em hardware, preste atenção na desmaterialização.”

Nunca esquecerei a frase de um conselheiro, capitão de um grande banco, sobre um novo concorrente que surgira no setor de pagamentos: “Espere e você verá, eles não comerão peru no Natal deste ano”. De alguma forma, esta frase reflete como grandes, ricas e gordas organizações enfrentam os novos concorrentes: com arrogncia.

A arrogncia dos grandes parece ser muito comum em nossa sociedade. Afinal, se são os grandes vitoriosos, eles devem ser os melhores naquilo que fazem, certo?

Na verdade, os líderes tendem a gastar muita energia para manter o status quo. Um amigo, executivo do setor de tecnologia, disse: “A Cielo passou os últimos dez anos impedindo o desenvolvimento do mercado…  Você não pode fazer uma joint venture entre uma empresa que quer desenvolver um mercado e outro cuja única estratégia é mantê-lo para si mesma.”

No livro ***As 22 Leis Imutáveis do Marketing***, os autores Al Ries e Jack Trout descrevem a Lei do Sucesso: “O sucesso frequentemente leva à arrogncia e a arrogncia, ao fracasso.” Acredito que as grandes credenciadoras vão reagir e usar todo o seu poder para se reinventar, trazendo inovações reais para o mercado. Na Cielo, especialmente, o novo CEO já fala da necessidade de mudança.

args.summary:
This article from Brazil Journal analyzes the competitive landscape of Brazil's card acquiring (payment processing) market, arguing that the industry is a commodity and the winners will be those who go beyond price competition to serve retailers' broader needs. The author identifies two key battlefronts: (1) offering financial services (credit, lower fees, collection services) and (2) providing technology (automation, software, sales-boosting apps). The article argues that POS terminals are obsolete and payments must become "invisible" and integrated.

The analysis of key players:
- **Stone:** Pioneered software + payments integration in Brazil. Has built a portfolio of companies offering reconciliation, split settlement, ERP, and financial services. Uses a costly "Stone HUB" localized sales force model to build brand recognition and reduce CAC over time, positioning it as a differentiator.
- **PagSeguro:** Born digital, targeting micro-merchants (MEIs) with mobile POS terminals and payment accounts. Over 70% transact monthly. Has its own bank and aims to become the bank for micro-merchants and SMBs, likely moving away from hardware to mobile payments.
- **New Players (Linx):** Software providers with large client bases entering payments via platforms like Linx Pay. The established leaders (Rede, GetNet) missed the opportunity to partner with Linx.
- **Current Leaders (Rede, Cielo):** Are criticized as laggards. Rede (owned by Itaú) is expected to lose market share to its own bank's share. Cielo is described as having done nothing disruptive, with its LIO hardware initiative going against the market trend of dematerialization.

The article concludes with a critique of incumbent arrogance, quoting the book "The 22 Immutable Laws of Marketing": "Success often leads to arrogance, and arrogance to failure." It notes the new CEO of Cielo acknowledges the need for change.

Boom in Mobile POS Adoption Across SMEs

Mobile POS installations climbed from 99,000 stores in 2015 to 350,000 stores by 2020 and have kept climbing as small and midsize merchants hunt for cost-efficient digital tools. Sumitomo Mitsui Card’s “next stera” roadmap seeks 1 million deployments by 2030, highlighting the scale of latent demand. Japan’s first MPoC-certified SoftPOS, launched through a Soft Space and GMO Financial Gate alliance, turns standard smartphones into secure payment devices.[2]GMO Financial Gate, “Soft Space and GMO-FG Capital Alliance,” gmo-fg.com Merchant appetite is lifted by lower hardware outlays, shorter rollout times, and value-added analytics that fixed terminals struggle to match. Regulatory pressure nudges the same direction because PCI DSS v4.0 encourages cloud orchestration over on-premise software. Together, economics and compliance converge to keep mobile POS at the core of the Japan POS terminals market expansion.

Surge in My-Number Linked Cashless Incentive Programs

The Cabinet Office aims for a 40% cashless ratio by 2025 and channels subsidies toward terminals capable of authenticating My-Number cards. Hospitals receive dedicated support to replace legacy machines so that insurance data, identity checks, and payment flows merge on one screen. Convenience chains mirror the push, retrofitting thousands of lanes to accept card-based identity verification at checkout. Local governments run QR campaigns tailored for seniors, reducing perceived complexity and stimulating terminal upgrades in community pharmacies and local grocers. Functionality now extends to automated tax reporting and loyalty aggregation, placing fresh performance demands on processors, memory, and encryption modules within each device. As a result, the Japan POS terminals market sees a durable boost anchored not in standard consumer spending cycles but in publicly funded modernization.

Growing QR-Code Interoperability (JPQR) Framework

JPQR’s roadmap toward full ASEAN linkage by 2025 obliges Japanese merchants to decode multiple QR formats and settle in varied currencies.[3]Japan Payment Service Association, “JPQR Framework and ASEAN Expansion,” j-psa.or.jp Vending operators, travel hubs, and luxury retailers upgrade firmware to parse domestic schemes alongside Singapore’s NETS or Thailand’s PromptPay. Tax-free shopping reforms scheduled for 2026 also require serial-number capture through POS for customs clearance, layering another compliance element on every scan. Terminal makers respond by embedding faster image sensors and optimizing QR decoding libraries so that scan times mimic tap-and-go convenience. The framework’s reach into transportation and hospitality extends total addressable volume beyond retail, pulling the Japan POS terminals market deeper into experiential commerce that hinges on speedy QR acceptance.

Upgrade Cycle Driven by PCI PTS v6.0 Compliance Deadline

PCI PTS v5.0 approvals sunset in 2029, yet Japan’s large retailers face an April 2026 deadline to shift to v6.0 hardware. Encryption algorithms, tamper-proof casings, and secure key-injection processes all tighten, rendering many pre-2020 terminals obsolete. Toshiba Tec has already booked replacement projects totaling 100,000 units for marquee chains and forecasts another wave once mid-tier merchants lock budgets. Though the mandate inflates near-term capex, it delivers predictable order flow for compliant vendors and raises entry barriers for low-cost imports that lack domestic certification. The Japan POS terminals market therefore enjoys a regulatory tailwind that reinforces technology refresh cycles.

Merchants face higher monthly fees for cloud analytics, tempering appetite for advanced software bundles. Enforcement clarity also remains fluid across credit, prepaid, and QR rails, creating legal ambiguity that slows procurement decisions. Initiatives such as the rollout of contactless readers across 20,000 ME-20 vending machines each year display how firmware upgrades can modernize sprawling installed bases without wholesale replacement. Once early hardware investment is amortized, merchants note throughput gains that translate into higher transaction volumes per store. Consumers report a preference for tap-and-go below USD 40, accelerating habit formation. As EMV tokenization matures, contactless also extends into mid-ticket categories, eating into contact dominance.

On the horizon, QR and contactless may converge as terminals juggle NFC and camera inputs on the same board. Vendors integrate dual readers plus software routing that picks the optimal rail depending on card scheme or wallet used. This multi-modal design lets chains hedge against evolving consumer tastes while controlling capital outlays. Because upgrade projects now aim for 7-year lifecycles, forward-compatible firmware proves a decisive purchasing factor. Fixed Point-of-Sale systems accrued 71.71% of 2025 revenue, reflecting deep roots in department stores and grocery chains that demand high-speed processing and tight ERP integration. Newer form factors are catching up; mobile and portable Point-of-Sale systems will grow 5.76% annually, catalyzed by SoftPOS models where the only hardware is a commodity smartphone. GMO Financial Gate’s stera tap is a flagship example, permitting large acquirers to onboard micro-merchants via an app download rather than a leased device. For service sectors like home repair or outdoor events, this mobility unshackles staff from counters, cuts queue times, and captures incremental sales.

Fixed devices nevertheless evolve. Toshiba Global Commerce Solutions unveiled the TCx 820 with six display sizes and the MxP Vision kiosk that pairs computer vision with AI item recognition. These systems address shrink management and self-checkout trends that remain beyond a phone’s capabilities. Consequently, both categories coexist, with mobile widening merchant reach and fixed units deepening functionality per square foot. The Japan POS terminals market therefore pivots not from one technology to the other but toward a layered stack where mobile and fixed complement one another depending on ticket size, vertical, and store format.

By End-User Industry: Healthcare Surges on Subsidy-Backed Upgrades

Retail captured 46.39% of 2025 revenue as convenience, department, and drug stores refreshed estates to enable omnichannel click-and-collect flows. Clinics and pharmacies rushing to meet 2025 policy deadlines must embed card readers plus secure ID modules that link treatment data to payment records. Vendors offer modular units with barcode, NFC, and fingerprint add-ons, ensuring future-proofing against additional regulatory layers.

Travel and hospitality also rebound as inbound tourism revives to pre-pandemic levels. Duty-free counters require POS systems that integrate with customs e-declaration APIs, and hotels seek multilingual menus to handle rising flows of ASEAN and European visitors. Transportation hubs integrate retail SKUs into transit payment ecosystems, extending the revenue surface area for each terminal. Education and government offices form a long tail of emerging adopters as citizen-service portals add fee collection through POS endpoints. These widening use cases consolidate demand curves that will keep the Japan POS terminals industry expanding even after retail replacement cycles decelerate.

Tokyo and Osaka dominate unit installations owing to dense merchant clusters, sustained tourist inflows, and early engagement with 5G and edge AI pilots. The success of 7-Eleven’s 500-store edge AI proof in Kanto illustrated how urban data velocity can unlock layered services that hinge on split-second image processing.

Regional cities such as Fukuoka and Sapporo follow behind, spurred by local grants that mirror national cashless targets. Their share of contactless taps is climbing faster than the national average, albeit from a smaller base, demonstrating convergence over the mid-term. Rural prefectures remain cash strongholds given higher senior ratios; thus merchants retain hybrid lanes that reconcile cash drawers with QR and IC card readers. Supply constraints in early-2024 delayed card issuance for rural transit networks, holding back associated POS procurement until chip supplies improved in September 2024.

Looking forward, Shinkansen station renovations and Expo 2025 Osaka are set to inject large terminal orders tied to retail concessions, ticketing, and hospitality suites. Coastal tourism belts aim for frictionless, tax-free checkout by 2026, prompting investment in multilingual and duty-free compliant terminals. Meanwhile, agriculture cooperatives exploring direct-to-consumer e-commerce are testing portable POS for farmers’ markets, illustrating how peripheral sectors enlarge the geographic footprint of the Japan POS terminals market.

Toshiba Tec holds about 50% domestic share, leveraging the ELERA platform, which added 200 companies and 2,300 stores year-over-year. NCR, PAX Global, and Samsung populate the next tier, focusing on specialized niches such as hospitality kiosks or Android-based handhelds. Competitive thrust centers on integrating computer-vision analytics, loyalty orchestration, and cloud dashboards that turn transaction streams into operational insights.

SoftPOS entrants disrupt from the bottom. The GMO Financial Gate and Soft Space alliance moved quickly to secure Japan’s first MPoC stamp, unlocking smartphone acceptance for micro-merchants and creating pressure on low-end hardware sales. Local fintechs NetStars and Recruit aim to bundle acquiring and marketing within unified apps, eroding value held by traditional ISO networks. Semiconductor vendors also step forward; Qualcomm’s tie-up with Toshiba Global Commerce Solutions packages AI inference at the edge, promising sub-200-millisecond object detection for self-checkout.

M&A and joint ventures shape the battlefield. NEC divested its hardware unit to Nihon Mirai Capital, indicating a pivot to software overlays rather than chassis manufacture. Toshiba Tec invested in TOUCH TO GO to gain unmanned micro-market capability, extending reach into grab-and-go formats. ## What is a POS system

A POS- or Point of Sale-system is a software and hardware complex that automates the daily business operations of cashiers and helps business owners track important sales data, such as inventory of goods and their value, sales growth, income, employee time accounting, etc. Simply put, POS is a central component of any business that involves paying for goods or services.

## 2024

### Global POS Terminal Market Size Reaches $113.38 Billion

At the end of 2024, the costs in the global POS terminal market amounted to $113.38 billion. More than a third of this amount was in the Asia-Pacific region. Industry trends are addressed in a study by Grand View Research, the results of which [TAdviser](/index.php/TAdviser "TAdviser") reviewed in early September 2025.

By POS terminals, analysts mean electronic devices designed to process financial transactions. These are hardware and software complexes that allow trading operations, as the traditional cash register does. Moreover, in addition to sales accounting, POS terminals can accumulate various data for their subsequent analysis.

![](/images/thumb/8/86/Po1s.jpg/840px-Po1s.jpg)

One of the drivers of the industry, the authors of the study call the growing popularity [of contactless payments](/index.php/Contactless_NFC_payments "Contactless NFC payments"). Enterprises in various fields are introducing [NFC-enabled](/index.php/NFC "NFC") devices that can interact with mobile payment systems. Companies actively use POS solutions to optimize operations, inventory management, control the movement of goods and effectively track sales.

The proliferation of mobile POS terminals has a stimulating impact on the market. The use of such equipment opens up new opportunities for small and medium-sized businesses. The integration of POS systems with data accounting and analysis [software](/index.php/Software "Software") is observed: this helps to improve the efficiency [of business processes](/index.php/BPM "BPM").

Another positive factor is the development of the Drive-Through concept, which allows customers to be served by [cars without](/index.php/Transport "Transport") forcing them to leave their vehicles. This model is widespread, in particular, in the segment of fast food restaurants and at gas stations. The Drive-Through concept began to gain popularity rapidly during the [COVID-19](/index.php/COVID-19 "COVID-19") pandemic, when people around the world faced severe coronavirus restrictions. The Drive-Through model involves the use of POS terminals, which leads to an increase in their sales.

The authors of the study segment the industry into stationary and mobile POS systems. In 2024, the first type of equipment provided the largest share of revenue - approximately 58%. Hardware solutions, software and services are distinguished by components: the main sales fell on the first of these segments - 62% in the total market volume. This is due, among other things, to the modernization of outdated systems in developing regions: enterprises in such countries are actively switching from traditional cash registers to modern POS systems against the background of government initiatives that stimulate digitalization, financial accessibility and the formalization of unorganized retail trade.

From a geographical point of view, in 2024, the Asia-Pacific region dominated, which accounted for 34.4% of the market in monetary terms. [North America's](/index.php/North_America "North America") share is estimated at 26%. In terms of the use of POS terminals, retail trade, catering establishments, [health care](/index.php?title=Pharmaceuticals,_Medicine,_Healthcare&action=edit&redlink=1 "Pharmaceuticals, Medicine, Healthcare (not exist)"), warehouse operations, entertainment, etc., are distinguished. In 2024, the first of these areas was in the lead. Globally, significant players are named:

Analysts at Grand View Research predict that in the future, the CAGR in the market under consideration will be 8.1%. Thus, by 2030, costs could increase to $181.47 billion.[[1]](#cite_note-0)

### The global market for smart payment terminals grew by 4% over the year and reached $56.36 billion

In 2024, costs in the global smart payment terminal market reached $56.36 billion. For comparison, in 2023, the volume of this market was estimated at $54.27 billion. Thus, an increase of about 4% was recorded. This is stated in a study by Market Research Future, the results of which [TAdviser](/index.php/TAdviser "TAdviser") got acquainted with in early March 2025.

By smart terminals, analysts mean devices with the ability to make transactions through [NFC](/index.php/NFC "NFC") and [QR codes](/index.php/QR "QR"), using [biometrics](/index.php?title=Information_Security_-_Biometric_Identification&action=edit&redlink=1 "Information Security - Biometric Identification (not exist)") and other modern technologies. The main drivers of the market in question are the growing popularity of various methods of digital payments and a surge in activity in the field of e-commerce. The COVID-19 pandemic has had a stimulating effect on the industry, increasing the need [for](/index.php/COVID-19 "COVID-19") contactless operations.

![](/images/6/6a/Payment.png)

The proliferation of mobile wallets and all kinds of Internet services creates additional demand for smart payment terminals. Consumers are increasingly shopping with their [smartphones](/index.php/Smartphone "Smartphone"): this is leading to an increase in dependence on e-commerce and online transactions. This shift in user behavior affects not only the retail sector, but also the hospitality, transportation and other industries.

Technological advances play an important role in expanding the market. Technologies such as [artificial intelligence](/index.php/Artificial_intelligence "Artificial intelligence"), [machine learning](/index.php/Machine_Learning "Machine Learning") and blockchain increase the functionality and security of payment terminals. Thanks to AI, companies can analyze consumer behavior, track transactions and prevent fraud. This helps to create a more secure payment environment, as well as increase customer satisfaction. Digital and mobile payments are gaining popularity in developing regions - expanding the geography of smart terminal sales, the study said. Analysts believe that over time, such equipment will become more and more complex functions.

The authors of the study identify five key market segments: NFC technology, magnetic stripe cards, EMV cards (jointly developed by Europay, [Mastercard](/index.php/Mastercard "Mastercard") and Visa payment systems), QR codes and [biometrics](/index.php?title=Information_Security_-_Biometric_Identification&action=edit&redlink=1 "Information Security - Biometric Identification (not exist)"). QR code payments are gaining popularity because they offer a convenient and effective way to make purchases without the need for cash or bank cards. Any smartphone with a camera is suitable for payment through a QR code - an NFC controller is not required. Technological innovations, including improved recognition of fingerprints, faces and iris, are driving the expansion of the biometric segment: mobile identification tools are becoming more efficient and reliable. [Geographically, North](/index.php/North_America "North America") America provides the largest revenue: the dominance of the region is due to the high level of development of [the](/index.php/North_America "North America") e-commerce sector, the active introduction of mobile banking and digital payments. This is followed by [Europe](/index.php/Europe "Europe") and the Asia-Pacific region.

Market Research Future analysts believe that in the future, the CAGR in the market under consideration will be 12.46%. As a result, costs globally could rise to $147.54 billion by 2032.[[2]](#cite_note-1)

## 2023: Global Wireless POS Terminal Market Growth to $2.15 Billion

In 2023, costs in the global wireless [POS](/index.php/POS "POS") terminal market amounted to $2.15 billion. This sector is showing steady positive dynamics, as stated in the Market Research Future review, published in mid-December 2024.

POS terminals are special devices that accept payment from buyers with bank cards and other electronic gadgets with contactless pairing, for example, smartphones or smartwatches. The terminals read the necessary information from the chip or magnetic strip of the card. Depending on the modification, such devices can support [NFC](/index.php/NFC "NFC") technology for contactless payment, [QR codes](/index.php/QR "QR") and (or) [biometrics](/index.php/Biometrics "Biometrics"). The POS terminal can be used as an [acquiring](/index.php/Article:Acquiring_(processing) "Acquiring (processing)") terminal or as a standalone device that makes online payments.

![](/images/0/00/Pos.png)

One of the main drivers of the market in question is the growing popularity of digital payments. Consumers are increasingly preferring mobile wallets and contactless payment methods, which stimulates sales of wireless POS terminals. Thanks to these devices, companies can accept payments anywhere and even on the go, which contributes to business development. The growing popularity of online retailers and mobile commerce is also having a positive impact on the industry. Businesses in sectors such as retail, restaurants and hospitality are increasingly using wireless POS terminals to serve customers.

The use of wireless communications eliminates the need for wired connections and infrastructure, reducing the cost of installing and maintaining equipment for enterprises. Such terminals are in demand among companies operating in remote areas or at temporary sites, for example, at certain events. Another market driver named technological advances, in particular, the integration of [artificial intelligence](/index.php/AI "AI") and [machine learning](/index.php/Machine_learning "Machine learning"): these technologies allow organizations to evaluate transaction data and receive information about consumer behavior and preferences. Plus, terminals with the ability to connect to cloud platforms are being introduced, which provides additional functionality, including remote management.

### Sales of POS terminals with NFC support - 47.8 million units

The volume of the global market for POS terminals with [NFC](/index.php/NFC "NFC") technology support in 2019 reached 47.8 million units, according to the research company Berg Insight. Analysts did not specify the dynamics regarding 2018, but said that sales of such equipment are on the rise, especially in [Europe](/index.php/Europe "Europe") and [North America](/index.php/North_America "North America").

In these two regions, about 94% of all POS terminals delivered per year supported the NFC standard. The technology has also become popular in markets such as [Brazil](/index.php/Brazil "Brazil"), [Turkey](/index.php/Turkey "Turkey") and [China](/index.php/China "China"). If we take deliveries of POS terminals around the world, then the share of NFC solutions in 2019 was 70%.

![](/images/thumb/1/11/300x160xkart2.jpg.pagespeed.ic.8IzYaWWNc9.jpg/840px-300x160xkart2.jpg.pagespeed.ic.8IzYaWWNc9.jpg)

Despite the increasing penetration of such equipment, in some cases contactless technology has not been activated. According to analysts, by the end of 2019, about 70 million POS devices around the world accepted contactless payments through [Visa payWave](/index.php/Company:Visa "Visa"), [[[Mastercard](/index.php/Mastercard "Mastercard")[[PayPass or [[UnionPay| PayPass or [UnionPay](/index.php/Company:UnionPay "UnionPay") Quickpass technologies.

The study notes that the key growth driver for the market in question is mobile terminals (mPOS). Their deliveries in 2019 reached 38.3 million units, taking 64% of the total volume of shipments.

In the mPOS segment, the share of NFC-enabled systems in 2019 was 64%, and sales of such equipment amounted to 24.7 million units.

Analysts only say that sales of such [software](/index.php/Software "Software") are growing and will increase due to the fact that the integration of applications like Shopify and QuickBooks is becoming more and more accessible. ## 2018: Trends in the development of POS systems

### Mobility

Among the latest trends in the development of POS systems can be distinguished by mobility. A mobile Point of Sale system or mPOS is a [tablet](/index.php/Tablet "Tablet") or [smartphone](/index.php/Smartphone "Smartphone") that acts as a traditional cash register or stationary POS system. Typically, mPOS [software](/index.php/Software "Software") is partially or completely deployed in the cloud and runs on mobile operating systems such as [iOS](/index.php/IOS "IOS"), [Android](/index.php/Product:Android "Android"), etc. Compared to traditional stationary POS devices, mPOS systems are more budget, compact and easy to use.

While traditional POS systems are mainly aimed at larger enterprises, mPOS is suitable for any business model from a startup to a wholesale company. In addition, mPOS systems will be a particularly profitable solution for representatives of small and medium-sized businesses, providing a low entry barrier for starting sales. The advantages of mobile POS systems and entrepreneurs with several outlets will be appreciated: portable mPOS devices are easy to transfer and use for settlement operations anywhere.

If we talk about security, then the mPOS systems are better than traditional POS transactions, since all mobile transactions are carefully encoded using point-to-point [encryption](/index.php/Enciphering "Enciphering") technology. By supplementing the mPOS system with a cloud solution, you can be sure that if your device is lost, stolen or broken, your data will be safe.

### Integrating POS with New Payment Types

The modern pace of life requires the purchase and sale operation to be as simple as possible, quickly and provide for several payment methods. With the advent of many convenient, fast and secure payment methods, it is not enough to simply accept payments with cash or bank cards. Together with existing and known payment types, the modern POS system should support the following payment methods:

[Mobile payment](/index.php/Mobile_payments "Mobile payments") apps allow customers to safely use credit and debit cards digitally with a mobile phone without having to carry them around at all times. If the POS system supports mobile payment, all a customer needs to do is simply attach a phone with [an NFC device](/index.php/NFC "NFC") or press the payment button on the phone.

For entrepreneurs, the mobile payment method is convenient in that it helps increase the speed of customer service, integrate [loyalty programs](/index.php?title=CRM_-_Loyalty_Systems&action=edit&redlink=1 "CRM - Loyalty Systems (not exist)") into [mobile payment applications](/index.php?title=Mobile_payment_apps&action=edit&redlink=1 "Mobile payment apps (not exist)") and track important sales data.

### Integration of POS systems with devices and services

A modern POS system cannot be imagined without integration with data collection devices such as a printer, magnetic card reader, pin code input device, cash register along with a cash box, [barcode](/index.php/Barcodes "Barcodes") scanner and other peripheral devices.

Each POS solution can also be integrated with different third-party services. Services such as payment system, shipping and delivery, gift certificates, sale of goods, discount program for regular customers, accounting system and much more are popular. These features can improve the efficiency of your POS system by turning it into a multifunctional solution.

### POS in various industries

Since each industry has its own characteristics, POS systems are developed taking into account the needs of each individual business. In general, POS systems will be particularly useful in [the](/index.php/Trade "Trade") retail, medical, hospitality and entertainment industries. The capabilities of modern POS solutions will help improve both customer and business experience[[5]](#cite_note-4).

# POS Terminals (Global Market) - Summary

This TAdviser article provides a comprehensive overview of the global POS (Point of Sale) terminal market, covering market size, trends, key players, and regional dynamics from 2018 to 2024.

## What is a POS System
A POS system is a software and hardware complex that automates cashier operations and helps business owners track sales data, inventory, income, and employee time accounting. It is a central component of any business involving payment for goods or services.

## 2024 Market Data
- **Global POS Terminal Market**: $113.38 billion (Grand View Research). Asia-Pacific accounted for 34.4%, North America 26%. CAGR projected at 8.1%, reaching $181.47 billion by 2030. Stationary POS systems provided ~58% of revenue; hardware solutions comprised 62% of total market volume.
- **Smart Payment Terminals**: $56.36 billion, up ~4% from $54.27 billion in 2023 (Market Research Future). CAGR of 12.46% projected, reaching $147.54 billion by 2032. North America leads in revenue.

## 2023 Market Data
- **Wireless POS Terminals**: $2.15 billion globally (Market Research Future). CAGR of 11.29% projected, reaching $5.71 billion by 2032. North America leads; Asia-Pacific shows fastest growth.

## 2020 Market Data
- Shipments of payment solutions grew 7.9% to 135 million units (The Nilson Report). Biometric terminals appeared for the first time in the sales structure. Key event: Ingenico acquired by a French payment services developer. In Europe (including Russia), 67% concentrated in 4 companies (Ingenico, PAX, Verifone, new entrants).

## 2019 Market Data
- **Global POS Terminal Market**: 24% growth in shipments to 128.2 million units. Chinese company Tianyu emerged as 2nd largest globally with 13.2 million units sold (217% increase). European market (including Russia) concentrated 73% in 4 companies.
- **NFC-enabled POS terminals**: 47.8 million units sold; 70% of all POS terminals shipped globally supported NFC. mPOS deliveries reached 38.3 million units (64% of total shipments). mPOS segment valued at $25.1 billion.
- **POS Software Market**: $1.1 billion globally (Juniper Research). China became the largest software market. Projected to reach $1.7 billion by 2024, with China accounting for 40%.

## 2018 Trends
- **Mobility**: mPOS systems (tablet/smartphone-based) gaining traction, especially for SMEs.
- **Integration with New Payment Types**: Mobile payments, NFC, biometrics, QR codes.
- **Integration with Devices and Services**: Printers, barcode scanners, payment systems, loyalty programs, accounting systems.
- **Industry-specific POS**: Retail, healthcare, hospitality, entertainment.

## Key Drivers
- Growing popularity of contactless payments and NFC technology
- Proliferation of mobile wallets and e-commerce
- COVID-19 pandemic accelerating contactless operations
- AI, machine learning, and blockchain enhancing functionality and security
- Drive-Through concept growth
- Government initiatives promoting digitalization

## Major Players
Ingenico, PAX Technology, Verifone, Newland, Tianyu (China), and others.

## Smart POS Market Outlook 2025-2034

The global **Smart POS market** was valued at **$28.6 billion** in 2025 and is projected to reach **$84.3 billion** by 2034, expanding at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of **12.8%** during the forecast period from 2026 to 2034, driven by accelerating contactless payment adoption, the proliferation of mobile commerce, and sweeping EMV compliance mandates across emerging economies. Smart point-of-sale systems represent the next generation of payment infrastructure, combining traditional transaction processing capabilities with cloud connectivity, advanced analytics, inventory management, customer relationship management (CRM) integration, and multi-modal payment acceptance including NFC, QR Code, EMV chip, and biometric authentication. The convergence of these technologies has fundamentally transformed the POS landscape from a pure transaction terminal into a comprehensive business intelligence and customer engagement platform. In 2025, the global retail sector processed an estimated **$32.4 trillion** in electronic payments, of which smart POS terminals intermediated approximately **$8.9 trillion**, underscoring the enormous untapped opportunity remaining in both developed and emerging markets. The shift away from traditional magnetic stripe and cash-based transactions toward chip-and-PIN, tap-and-go, and QR-code-based payments has been the single most powerful structural tailwind sustaining Smart POS demand growth since 2021. Regulatory frameworks have also played a decisive role: the Reserve Bank of India's mandate for EMV migration, the European Union's PSD2 directive requiring strong customer authentication, and similar regulatory pushes across Southeast Asia and Latin America collectively accelerated terminal upgrade cycles, adding an estimated **42 million** new smart POS units to the global installed base in 2024 and 2025 alone. Cloud-based POS architectures have further unlocked recurring software-as-a-service (SaaS) revenue streams, with leading vendors now deriving between **30%** and **55%** of their total revenue from subscriptions rather than hardware sales, a structural shift that has dramatically improved margin profiles and long-term revenue visibility. Increasing smartphone penetration, particularly in Asia Pacific and Sub-Saharan Africa, has simultaneously validated the mobile POS (M-POS) segment as a powerful democratizing force, bringing formal payment infrastructure to micro-merchants, street vendors, and small businesses previously excluded from electronic commerce ecosystems. As 5G networks roll out globally and edge computing reduces latency for real-time fraud detection and analytics, the Smart POS market is poised for an unprecedented decade of innovation and growth through 2034.

## Smart POS Market Regional Outlook 2025-2034

**Asia Pacific** represented the largest regional market for Smart POS in 2025, accounting for **$10.35 billion** or **36.2%** of global revenues. The region's dominance is rooted in the extraordinary scale and velocity of digital payment adoption across China, India, Japan, South Korea, and emerging Southeast Asian economies. China alone hosts the world's most sophisticated mobile payment ecosystem, with Alipay and WeChat Pay having collectively processed over **$17 trillion** in QR-code-based payments in 2024, creating an enormous installed base demand for QR-code-enabled Smart POS terminals. India's government-led push under the Digital India initiative and the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) platform drove Smart POS terminal activations by an estimated **28%** year-on-year in 2024 and 2025, with Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities emerging as the fastest-growing subsectors. South Korea and Japan, already highly saturated in contactless payment acceptance, are driving demand for next-generation biometric-enabled terminals and integrated loyalty management systems. The broader Southeast Asian market, encompassing Indonesia, Vietnam, Thailand, the Philippines, and Malaysia, collectively posted Smart POS adoption rates exceeding **19%** annually between 2022 and 2025, underpinned by central bank interoperability mandates, fintech investment flows, and rapidly expanding e-commerce logistics networks that require sophisticated last-mile payment solutions. Asia Pacific is forecast to maintain a leading CAGR of **14.1%** through 2034, retaining its dominant position throughout the forecast period.

**North America** was the second-largest regional market in 2025, accounting for approximately **28.4%** of global Smart POS revenues, driven primarily by the United States where large-format retail, quick-service restaurant (QSR) chains, and healthcare providers have collectively committed to large-scale POS modernization programs. The U.S. market benefited from the EMV liability shift that accelerated terminal upgrades across millions of small and medium-sized businesses, while the appetite for cloud-based, data-analytics-rich POS ecosystems has remained exceptionally strong. Canada similarly posted robust growth, with its near-universal contactless payment acceptance rate (above **88%** of all in-store transactions in 2025) providing fertile ground for Smart POS terminal upgrades and software layer monetization. The restaurant segment, encompassing both full-service and quick-service dining, accounted for the highest share of new Smart POS deployments in North America in 2025, as operators sought to integrate ordering, payment, loyalty, and kitchen display workflows into unified smart terminal ecosystems. North America's market is projected to expand at a CAGR of **11.3%** between 2026 and 2034, sustained by ongoing software subscription revenue growth and the penetration of biometric payment authentication in high-security verticals including healthcare and financial services.

**Europe** commanded approximately **22.6%** of global Smart POS revenues in 2025, anchored by mature markets in the United Kingdom, Germany, France, and the Nordic countries where contactless payment penetration has exceeded **75%** of all point-of-sale transactions. The EU's PSD2 strong customer authentication (SCA) requirements, which became fully enforced across all member states by 2023, created a sustained upgrade cycle that pushed millions of legacy terminals out of compliance, directly fueling demand for EMV-compliant and NFC-enabled Smart POS hardware. Eastern Europe represents a rapidly growing subregion, with countries including Poland, Czech Republic, Romania, and Hungary posting Smart POS adoption growth rates between **16%** and **21%** annually as banking infrastructure modernizes. **Latin America** held approximately **7.8%** of global market share in 2025, with Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia leading regional adoption. Brazil's Pix instant payment system, launched by the Banco Central do Brasil, generated an enormous wave of QR-code POS terminal upgrades among small merchants, processing over **42 billion** transactions in 2024. The **Middle East and Africa** region accounted for approximately **5.0%** of global revenues in 2025 but is forecast to post the second-highest regional CAGR of **15.6%** through 2034, driven by fintech-led financial inclusion initiatives across Sub-Saharan Africa, GCC nations' Vision 2030/2035 programs prioritizing cashless economies, and rapid smartphone penetration enabling M-POS as the primary commerce infrastructure for underbanked populations.

## Smart POS Market Key Growth Drivers 2025-2034

### Surging Global Adoption of Contactless and NFC Payments

The most powerful structural driver behind Smart POS market growth is the global pivot toward contactless payment methods, with near-field communication (NFC) technology serving as the primary enabler at the point of sale. Global contactless payment transaction volumes surpassed **$4.6 trillion** in 2024 and are projected to exceed **$14 trillion** by 2033, implying a sustained expansion that directly necessitates Smart POS terminal upgrades across every retail, hospitality, and services vertical. In markets such as the United Kingdom, Australia, and Singapore, contactless transactions already account for more than **90%** of all card-present payments, establishing a clear benchmark for where global transaction behavior is heading. Consumer preference surveys conducted across **18 countries** in 2025 revealed that **74%** of respondents preferred contactless payment options over inserting or swiping cards, citing speed, hygiene, and convenience as primary motivators. Smart POS terminals equipped with NFC antennas also support a broader range of digital wallets including Apple Pay, Google Pay, Samsung Pay, and domestic wallet ecosystems, dramatically expanding the addressable payment surface at any given merchant location. The integration of dynamic currency conversion, split-bill functionality, and real-time loyalty point crediting within NFC-enabled Smart POS ecosystems has further elevated the consumer experience, driving repeat purchase behavior that merchants strongly value. Industry data from 2025 suggests that merchants deploying NFC-enabled Smart POS terminals experienced an average **11.3%** increase in average basket size compared to those operating legacy swipe terminals, providing a compelling business case for rapid hardware refresh cycles.

### Expansion of the Informal Economy and SME Digital Payment Adoption

Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and micro-merchants represent the single largest untapped opportunity within the global Smart POS ecosystem, comprising an estimated **512 million** business entities worldwide that still rely primarily on cash transactions as of 2025. The proliferation of low-cost M-POS dongles, cloud-connected smart terminals, and QR-code-based payment acceptance solutions has dramatically reduced the barrier to entry for electronic payment acceptance, with entry-level Smart POS hardware now available at price points as low as **$29** to **$49** for compact M-POS devices in competitive markets such as India, Brazil, and Indonesia. Fintech companies including Square (Block Inc.), SumUp, iZettle, and regional players such as Paytm and MercadoPago have aggressively expanded their smart terminal ecosystems with bundled services including working capital lending, inventory tracking, and payroll management, creating powerful network effects that lock merchants into recurring service relationships. Government-backed digital payment promotion programs across **47 countries** tracked in 2025 provided direct subsidies or zero-interest financing for smart terminal procurement by qualifying SMEs, injecting an estimated **$2.1 billion** in cumulative public capital into terminal expansion between 2023 and 2025. As related infrastructure including telecom electronic manufacturing services continues to scale, the cost of connectivity-embedded Smart POS hardware is expected to decline by a further **18-22%** by 2028, further accelerating SME adoption in cost-sensitive markets.

### EMV Migration Mandates and Regulatory-Driven Terminal Upgrade Cycles

Regulatory mandates for EMV chip-and-PIN compliance have been one of the most reliable and recurring demand generators for Smart POS hardware globally, creating predictable replacement cycles every five to seven years as liability shift policies are implemented and enforced. EMVCo reported that **96.4%** of card-present transactions processed globally in 2024 were on EMV-compliant terminals, up from **68.2%** in 2018, yet the residual **3.6%** non-compliant transaction base still represents hundreds of millions of legacy terminals requiring replacement. More significantly, the expiry of existing EMV hardware generations, combined with evolving security certification requirements such as PCI DSS 4.0 (fully effective March 2025) and new Kernel 3 contactless specifications from EMVCo, is creating fresh mandatory upgrade waves even in already-EMV-compliant markets. PCI DSS 4.0, which introduced 64 new or substantially revised requirements for cardholder data environments, has compelled payment processors and acquiring banks to trigger accelerated terminal refresh programs across their merchant portfolios, with an estimated **$3.8 billion** in compliance-driven Smart POS procurement budgeted across North America and Europe for 2025 and 2026 combined. Biometric authentication requirements for high-value transactions in markets such as Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and India are additionally driving demand for next-generation Smart POS terminals equipped with fingerprint and facial recognition modules, a segment growing at an estimated **24.3%** CAGR in isolation through 2030.

### Cloud-Based SaaS Ecosystems and Data-Driven Merchant Intelligence

The transformation of Smart POS from a transactional hardware device into a cloud-connected merchant intelligence platform represents perhaps the most consequential long-term value creation driver in the market. The integration of Smart POS data streams with enterprise resource planning (ERP) and customer data platforms is increasingly standard among enterprise retailers, creating deep system dependencies that generate long-term vendor lock-in and recurring revenue predictability. These software ecosystem dynamics are attracting significant venture capital and private equity investment into Smart POS platform companies, with global investment in POS technology companies exceeding **$4.9 billion** in 2024 alone.

## What is a Smart POS terminal and how does it differ from a traditional POS system?

A Smart POS terminal is a next-generation payment and commerce management device that combines payment processing hardware with a cloud-connected operating system, application marketplace, and analytics capabilities, typically running on Android or Linux platforms with cellular or Wi-Fi connectivity. Unlike traditional legacy POS systems that performed only transactional functions via closed, proprietary architectures, Smart POS terminals support NFC contactless payments, EMV chip cards, QR code scanning, and biometric authentication while simultaneously running business applications including inventory management, loyalty programs, and real-time sales reporting. In 2025, the global installed base of Smart POS terminals reached an estimated **215 million** units, compared to approximately **88 million** in 2020, reflecting the rapid displacement of legacy hardware. The software-driven revenue model of Smart POS ecosystems, where vendors earn recurring SaaS fees in addition to hardware margins, distinguishes them fundamentally from traditional POS manufacturers that relied solely on hardware sales and proprietary support contracts.

## Smart POS Market Analysis by Technology

The **NFC (Near Field Communication)** technology segment was the largest in the Smart POS market in 2025, representing approximately **41.5%** of total revenues. NFC technology's dominance is a direct reflection of the global shift toward contactless payment as the preferred consumer transaction modality, encompassing not just card-based tap-to-pay but also digital wallet payments via smartphones, smartwatches, and wearables. NFC-enabled Smart POS terminals have become the de facto standard in Western Europe, North America, Australia, and advanced APAC markets, where virtually all new terminal deployments are NFC-capable. The technology's reliability, transaction speed (typically under **500 milliseconds** per transaction), and broad device compatibility have made it the payment engineer's and consumer's preferred first choice at physical checkout. Key NFC chipset manufacturers supplying Smart POS OEMs include NXP Semiconductors, STMicroelectronics, and Broadcom, with NXP maintaining a leading market position estimated at approximately **60%** of the NFC semiconductor supply chain for payment terminals. The growing integration of NFC with loyalty card emulation, transit ticketing, and digital ID verification is broadening the NFC Smart POS use case beyond pure payment into composite identity and commerce services, further entrenching NFC's market leadership through 2034. The NFC segment is forecast to grow at a CAGR of **12.1%** through 2034. The **EMV** technology segment held approximately **31.2%** market share in 2025, representing the core chip-and-PIN and chip-and-signature payment standard that has been the backbone of global payment security since the mid-2010s. EMV's share of the Smart POS technology mix is expected to gradually decline in relative percentage terms as NFC and QR Code solutions capture proportionally larger shares of new deployments, though the absolute EMV hardware market will continue to grow as terminal upgrade cycles in Asia, Latin America, and Africa replace legacy magnetic stripe infrastructure with EMV-compliant units.

The **QR Code** technology segment accounted for approximately **19.3%** of Smart POS market revenues in 2025 and represents the fastest-growing technology segment with a forecast CAGR of **16.7%** through 2034. QR code-based payment acceptance has experienced extraordinary growth in Asia Pacific, particularly in China and India, where super-app ecosystems have standardized QR code payment at virtually every merchant type from street vendors to luxury retailers. Brazil's Pix instant payment system, which processes QR code transactions, and similar real-time payment rails being deployed across Southeast Asia, Mexico, and Europe are extending QR code's reach well beyond Asia into global markets previously dominated by card-based payment. Smart POS terminals that support QR code payment acceptance require dynamic QR code generation capabilities, camera or scanner modules, and real-time connectivity to payment processing networks, capabilities increasingly standard on Android-based smart terminal platforms. The **Biometrics** technology segment, while the smallest at approximately **8.0%** of market share in 2025, is projected to be the fastest-growing sub-category at a CAGR of **24.3%** through 2034, driven by the deployment of fingerprint-authenticated payment in India, facial recognition payment pilots in China and South Korea, and palm-vein recognition systems being rolled out by Amazon in its retail network. Biometric payment authentication in Smart POS environments addresses both security and friction reduction goals simultaneously, eliminating the need for PIN entry while providing cryptographic-grade transaction authorization. The broader semiconductor ecosystem enabling biometric Smart POS includes advanced sensor arrays similar to those studied in the MEMS microelectromechanical systems market, where miniaturization and cost reduction trajectories are favorable for widespread deployment.

## What is the difference between NFC and QR Code payment technology in Smart POS systems?

NFC (Near Field Communication) payment in Smart POS systems works by establishing a wireless radio frequency communication link between the terminal and a payment device (card, phone, or wearable) within a range of approximately **4 centimeters**, enabling instantaneous, hardware-secured transaction authorization without requiring internet connectivity for the consumer's device. QR Code payment, by contrast, relies on either the merchant generating a static or dynamic QR code that the consumer scans with their smartphone camera, or the consumer displaying a QR code from their wallet app that the terminal scans, with the transaction settled through a real-time payment network that requires both parties to have internet connectivity. NFC dominated the global Smart POS technology mix in 2025 with a **41.5%** share, while QR Code held **19.3%** but is growing at a faster CAGR of **16.7%** versus NFC's **12.1%** through 2034, reflecting QR Code's lower infrastructure cost and its suitability for markets with high smartphone penetration but lower card ownership rates. Both technologies are increasingly co-implemented on the same Smart POS terminal platform, with leading vendors such as Ingenico, PAX Technology, and VeriFone shipping multi-modal devices that support NFC, EMV, QR Code, and magnetic stripe acceptance simultaneously to maximize merchant payment acceptance coverage.

## Smart POS Market Opportunities and Threats 2025-2034

The Smart POS market presents a rich landscape of growth opportunities across both hardware and software dimensions in 2025 and the years ahead. The most compelling near-term opportunity lies in the conversion of the estimated **512 million** cash-dependent micro-merchants and SMEs worldwide into the formal electronic payment ecosystem through low-cost M-POS and QR-code-based acceptance solutions. This represents a multi-decade conversion opportunity with a very long runway, particularly in Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, and Southeast Asia where smartphone penetration is rising rapidly but bank branch density remains low. The healthcare vertical presents another high-value growth opportunity for Smart POS vendors: hospital systems and outpatient clinics in the United States, Western Europe, and developed APAC markets are collectively investing billions of dollars in patient-facing digital payment infrastructure, with Smart POS terminals serving as the physical commerce touchpoint for co-pay collection, prescription payment, and health savings account (HSA) card processing. The integration of Smart POS terminals with electronic health record (EHR) systems enables automated insurance verification and co-pay calculation at the point of care, dramatically reducing billing errors and improving collection rates. The growing self-service and autonomous retail trend represents a third major opportunity vector, with integrated Smart POS modules embedded in unmanned micro-markets, smart vending machines, automated fueling stations, and grab-and-go convenience formats expected to add tens of millions of new payment acceptance touchpoints globally between 2025 and 2034. Software and ecosystem monetization represents perhaps the most structurally significant long-term opportunity, as vendors shift from hardware margin dependency toward high-margin recurring SaaS subscription revenues from analytics, loyalty management, payroll, lending, and third-party app marketplace curation. Smart POS vendors that successfully build application marketplace ecosystems similar to those pioneered by Square, Toast, and Clover stand to capture disproportionate long-term value creation relative to pure hardware providers. The convergence of Smart POS with automated test equipment protocols for self-diagnostic payment terminal management is also opening new opportunities in remote terminal monitoring, predictive maintenance, and zero-touch deployment, reducing total cost of ownership for large merchant fleets.

Emerging market financial inclusion programs, specifically the aggressive push by governments and development finance institutions to digitize informal market transactions, represent an additional category of opportunity with strong tailwinds from public policy and multilateral development bank investment. The World Bank's Financial Inclusion Global Initiative and similar programs from the Asian Development Bank and IFC have collectively committed over **$3.2 billion** to digital payment infrastructure development in emerging markets between 2023 and 2027, with Smart POS hardware procurement representing a direct beneficiary of these funding flows. Cross-border payment acceptance through Smart POS is a fast-emerging use case, particularly in tourism-heavy markets where accepting multiple foreign digital wallets, including Alipay, WeChat Pay, and regional alternatives, at hotel, restaurant, and attraction POS terminals represents a direct revenue enhancement opportunity for merchants. As international travel volumes recovered past pre-pandemic levels by 2024 and surpassed them in 2025, Smart POS vendors offering plug-and-play cross-border digital wallet acceptance saw disproportionately strong demand from the hospitality and travel retail sectors. Furthermore, the build-out of smart city infrastructure globally is creating new integrated Smart POS deployment opportunities in public transit, parking, and government service payment kiosks, with vendors possessing ruggedized, outdoor-rated terminal form factors and long-term service agreements well-positioned to capture significant public sector contract value.

Despite robust growth prospects, the Smart POS market faces several meaningful threats that participants must navigate carefully. Cybersecurity vulnerabilities represent the most acute and persistent threat, as smart payment terminals connected to cloud networks present a significantly larger attack surface than legacy closed-system POS hardware, with point-of-sale malware attacks estimated to have compromised over **47 million** payment card credentials globally in 2024 according to security research firm Gemini Advisory. Regulatory and compliance complexity poses a related challenge: the simultaneous evolution of PCI DSS standards, EMVCo certification requirements, national payment scheme mandates, and data privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA, PDPA) creates a compliance burden that smaller Smart POS vendors may struggle to manage, potentially consolidating the market further toward well-resourced incumbents. Supply chain disruptions, particularly for semiconductor components critical to Smart POS hardware manufacturing (NFC chips, secure elements, application processors), remain a structural vulnerability following the disruptions of 2021-2023, with geopolitical tensions around semiconductor manufacturing geography adding ongoing uncertainty. Pricing pressure from low-cost Chinese manufacturers, particularly PAX Technology, Newland Payment, and SZZT Electronics, continues to compress hardware margins globally, challenging Western vendors to differentiate on software ecosystem depth and security certification credentials. The risk of platform disintermediation by major digital wallet providers (Apple, Google, Samsung) seeking to integrate payment processing directly within their mobile ecosystems, potentially bypassing traditional Smart POS hardware entirely in contactless-dominant markets, represents a longer-term structural threat to conventional terminal hardware demand in mature markets.

The top five vendors, consisting of Ingenico (Worldline), VeriFone, PAX Technology, Newland Payment, and Clover Network (Fiserv), collectively accounted for an estimated **48.3%** of global Smart POS hardware revenues in 2025, while the software and services layer remains substantially more fragmented with hundreds of ISV (independent software vendor) ecosystems operating across vertical markets and geographies. #### Point of Sale (POS) Terminal Market Size in Japan: Key Research Findings 2024Domestic POS Terminal Market Holds Steady at Around 100,000 Units, Anticipating Replacement Demand from Convenience Store Chains Post-FY2026

Yano Research Institute (the President, Takashi Mizukoshi) conducted a survey on the domestic point-of-sale (POS) terminal market and found out the trends of retail solutions, strategies of POS system related enterprises, and future outlook of the market.

**Domestic POS Terminal Market Size Forecast**

![Domestic POS Terminal Market Size Forecast](http://www.yanoresearch.com/press/images/3641_0.jpg)

## Market Overview

The domestic POS terminal market showed a recovery as distribution and retail companies resumed investment in systems, which had been held off during the covid crisis. As a result, the shipment volume of the POS terminal market attained 96,773 units in FY022, 106.4% of the previous year.  However, the shipment by value fell below the previous year to 37,639 million yen (94.0% on the same basis).  
 The recovery trend was even more pronounced in FY2023, with shipment volume reaching 107,837 units (111.4%). Moreover, affected by the recent inflation, as well as by the rise in the unit price of POS system due to the spread of self-checkout POS terminals, the shipment value grew to 45,221 million yen (120.1%).

## Noteworthy Topics

### A Rise of Self-Checkout Backed by Serious Labor Shortage

A serious labor shortage in the retail distribution industry is urging the stores to find ways to cut down on manual operations, especially those regarding checkout and product merchandising. Under the circumstances, demand for semi-self-checkout may be replaced by the demand for full self-checkout, which eliminates the need for manual operation. In addition, owing to a patent right, a limited number of IT vendors can provide a semi-self-checkout system. Consequently, vendors will be competing against each other in the development of a full self-checkout system, thus making it a primary option for user companies.   
   
 In addition to the traditional stationary self-checkout system, two new POS checkout systems are emerging: smart carts and mobile POS using smartphones. A smart cart is mainly a self-checkout system with a tablet computer mounted on the cart. Mobile POS is a self-checkout system that allows customers to read tags with their smartphone or with a store-owned smartphone. Going forward, the demand for these types of checkout systems is expected to rise significantly as it enables the reduction of checkers to the minimum.

## Future Outlook

Since the market cannot expect considerable growth except when major retail chains upgrade their checkout systems, the demand for domestic POS terminals is projected to remain flat or shrink gradually.  
 The market size of POS terminal is expected to decline in FY2024 to 107,410 units (99.6% of the previous fiscal year) by shipment volume. Nevertheless, owing to the replacement of self-service checkout machines, it is forecasted to grow to 47,395 million yen (104.8% of the previous fiscal year) by shipment value. While the market size by volume is predicted to stay at 112,781 units (105%) for FY2025, it will drop to 42,857 million yen (90.4%) by value due to a decline in the unit price of self-service cash registers stemming from intensifying competition.  
 Substantial market growth is anticipated in FY2026 and FY2027. Given that the previous POS system upgrades at the three major chains occurred nearly at the same time, the next round of replacements is expected to follow a similar timeline.  
 By reason of the above, the shipment volume is expected to expand to 135,337 units in FY2026 (120.0% of the previous fiscal year) and 175,938 units by FY2027 (130.0%). The shipment value is forecasted to reach 51,428 million for FY2026 (120.0%) and 70,375 million for FY2027 (136.8%).

1.Research Period： June to September 2024  
 2.Research Object： Businesses related to POS system (POS terminal manufacturers, POS software vendors, tablet POS system vendors), mission-critical system vendors, demand forecasting/automatic ordering system vendors, online grocery store system vendors, major user companies (system persons of leading mass merchandisers, etc.)   
 3.Research Methogology： Face-to-face interviews by our specialized researchers (including online interviews), interview via telephone/email, and literature research

**What is Point of Sale Terminal Market?**

A POS (point of sale) is a sales management system that manages and tabulates merchandize sales by item at the place at which goods are retailed, which is comprised of servers, POS terminals, POS software, and other peripheral devices.  
 In this research, the market size of POS terminals (by volume and value) is calculated based on the shipment of POS terminals at manufacturers.

- Merchant budget pressure and hardware commoditization
- Security, certification, and regulatory complexity
- Fragmented integration and legacy installed base

MyData 2.0 widened data-sharing to offline channels in 2025 and lowered the minimum user age to 14, prompting merchants to install age-verification modules. Real-time payments hit 9.1 billion in 2023 and continue to scale, making compliance with QR and NFC standards mandatory for merchants.

Expansion of E-commerce-Driven Omni-Channel Fulfilment

Online channels captured 50.6% of total retail sales in 2024, up from 47.3% in 2023. Retailers now deploy POS networks that synchronize stock across stores, warehouses, and click-and-collect points, enabling same-day delivery. Persistent Data-Security and Cyber-Fraud Concerns

The August 2025 Lotte Card breach leaked data on 2.97 million users, spotlighting vulnerabilities and triggering demand for PCI-PTS 6.x hardware encryption. SK Telecom’s USIM hack the same year forced regulators to tighten wallet oversight. Revised enforcement decrees now impose stricter capital and transaction ceilings on payment gateways. Budget-constrained merchants, however, often delay upgrades because secure processors add cost and integration complexity.

Government cashless incentives and falling unit prices, however, will narrow the gap, making contactless acceptance mainstream before 2031. The South Korea POS terminals market size for contactless solutions is therefore poised to expand meaningfully, provided subsidy frameworks offset merchant upgrade expenses.

As EMVCo-aligned QR rolls out nationwide, retailers gain an immediate path to contactless payments without buying new readers. Bank of Korea’s ISO 20022 settlement rails give acquirers faster fund availability, improving merchant cash flow. Meanwhile, GS1 mandates on QR and DataMatrix codes for variable-weight goods oblige scanner upgrades, further encouraging retailers to adopt dual-mode terminals. Cloud deployments, however, are growing at 7.48% annually, propelled by real-time sync and remote updates. Incheon International Airport, a gateway for more than 50 million annual travelers, catalyzes hospitality upgrades, including biometric checkout at Lotte Duty Free. Cloud migration projects such as GS Retail’s finance overhaul show how centralized data architecture can harmonize processes across 17 provinces, narrowing earlier capability gaps.

South Korea's POS terminal ecosystem is shaped by electronic payment and data-security obligations that affect both hardware refresh cycles and software design. The Financial Services Commission oversees electronic financial transactions, including information-security requirements for financial entities and payment intermediaries, while the Korea Internet and Security Agency (KISA) supports information-security standards and assessment functions under the Ministry of Science and ICT.

At the acceptance layer, terminals used for card payments rely on security certification practices supported by industry bodies such as the Credit Finance Association of Korea. This reinforces the shift toward IC cards and encrypted processing and sustains demand for newer secure terminal specifications after high-profile fraud and breach events. Hardware vendors provide countertop and mobile terminals with secure elements and IC/EMV capabilities, while POS software providers and integrators deliver Android-based smart POS, cloud dashboards, and connectors that link to inventory, loyalty, kiosk, and analytics modules.

Transaction routing and merchant onboarding are handled primarily through VAN providers and acquirers that connect terminals to card networks and bank settlement. They also run mandatory security testing and certification workflows before devices can process card payments. Downstream, merchants across retail, hospitality, healthcare, and logistics drive requirements such as QR acceptance, digital receipts, and e-invoicing compliance, which increases the share of recurring software and services (device management, security updates, and data analytics) alongside continued hardware replacement cycles.

NHN KCP’s KCP Order, which lets merchants rely on QR codes or NFC stickers, demonstrates disruptive potential by slashing hardware expenses. ## Market Opportunities and Future Outlook

The most visible opportunity is in subsidized smart-store upgrades for SMEs, where cost and compliance requirements are pushing merchants toward newer terminals, kiosks, and software-led POS stacks. The government's Smart Store Technology Dissemination Project supports adoption through subsidies that can cover 70% of costs (up to 80% for vulnerable groups such as simple taxpayers and single-person businesses), covering purchase, rental, and software-based models and giving vendors a pathway to bundle terminals with subscriptions and managed services.

Compliance-driven redesign is also creating whitespace in accessibility-ready unmanned terminals and integrated checkout. As of January 28, 2025, the Small Business Market Promotion Corporation requires barrier-free accessibility features for new unmanned terminals and kiosks installed at workplaces with fewer than 100 employees, encouraging replacements and feature upgrades such as voice output and wheelchair access that domestic OEMs and integrators can package into recurring offerings. In parallel, offline payment ecosystem expansion by major platforms and banks, including merchant terminal support programs and integrated offline terminals, continues to support demand for QR and NFC-capable devices and tighter integration between POS software, settlement accounts, and loyalty ecosystems.

## Recent Industry Developments

* July 2026: Naver Pay announced that its Npay Connect offline integrated payment terminal exceeded 100,000 merchant locations. The expansion of offline merchant footprint strengthens the terminal ecosystem and improves network effects in the South Korea merchant base.
* July 2026: Rocket Pay offline expansion to brick-and-mortar retail stores. The move broadens Coupang’s payment rails beyond e-commerce, increasing merchant lock-in and data capture.
* July 2026: Merchant terminal purchase subsidy program in partnership with Toss Place. The program accelerates market-wide terminal upgrades by subsidizing new terminals for SMEs and captures settlement volume through banks.
