* [2. How Much Does Clover Flex Cost?](#How_Much_Does_Clover_Flex_Cost)
  + [2.1. When the Higher Tiers Pay for Themselves](#When_the_Higher_Tiers_Pay_for_Themselves)
* [3. Clover Flex vs. Flex Pocket: Which One Do You Need?](#Clover_Flex_vs_Flex_Pocket_Which_One_Do_You_Need)
* [4. Clover Flex Specs](#Clover_Flex_Specs)
  + [4.1. Why the Flex Has Better Internals Than the Station Duo](#Why_the_Flex_Has_Better_Internals_Than_the_Station_Duo)
* [5. Battery Life and Daily Use](#Battery_Life_and_Daily_Use)
* [6. How Clover Flex Compares to Other Clover Devices](#How_Clover_Flex_Compares_to_Other_Clover_Devices)
* [7. Clover Flex vs. Square Terminal](#Clover_Flex_vs_Square_Terminal)
* [8. Who Should Buy the Clover Flex?](#Who_Should_Buy_the_Clover_Flex)
  + [8.1. ✅ Good fit for](#_Good_fit_for)
  + [8.2. ❌ Not ideal for](#_Not_ideal_for)
* [9. Frequently Asked Questions](#Frequently_Asked_Questions)
  + [9.1. How much does Clover Flex cost?](#How_much_does_Clover_Flex_cost)
  + [9.2. What's the difference between Clover Flex and Flex Pocket?](#Whats_the_difference_between_Clover_Flex_and_Flex_Pocket)
  + [9.3. How long does the Clover Flex battery last?](#How_long_does_the_Clover_Flex_battery_last)
  + [9.4. Does the Clover Flex print receipts?](#Does_the_Clover_Flex_print_receipts)
  + [9.5. Can Clover Flex work with a cash drawer?](#Can_Clover_Flex_work_with_a_cash_drawer)
  + [9.6. Does Clover Flex work without WiFi?](#Does_Clover_Flex_work_without_WiFi)
  + [9.7. Is Clover Flex better than Clover Station Duo?](#Is_Clover_Flex_better_than_Clover_Station_Duo)
  + [9.8. Does the $450 Clover promo apply to the Flex?](#Does_the_450_Clover_promo_apply_to_the_Flex)
  + [9.9. Can I use a Clover Flex with a different payment processor?](#Can_I_use_a_Clover_Flex_with_a_different_payment_processor)
  + [9.10. Can Clover Flex scan barcodes?](#Can_Clover_Flex_scan_barcodes)
* [10. Our Verdict](#Our_Verdict)

---

The Clover Flex is a handheld POS terminal with a 5.99″ touchscreen, built-in receipt printer, and at least 8 hours of battery for typical small business use. It costs $749 upfront or $40 per month on a 36-month plan. Unlike Clover’s countertop devices, it goes wherever the payment happens: tableside, curbside, in line, or out on a job.

The current model is the Flex 4, and it’s the most modern hardware Clover sells. It runs Android 13 with 4 GB of RAM and 64 GB of storage, which is a generation ahead of the Station Duo and Station Solo. The cheapest full-featured device in the lineup is also the newest one, which is unusual and worth knowing before you spend $1,899 on a countertop station.

This page covers the device itself: what it costs, how it differs from the Flex Pocket, the specs that matter, and who it fits. For Clover’s software plans in depth, processing details, contract terms, and company reputation, see our full [Clover POS review](https://www.posusa.com/clover-pos-review/).

**🎯 Limited Time Offer:** New merchants can get up to $450 off Clover hardware, and both the Flex and Flex Pocket are eligible devices. [See the $450 Clover promo details](https://www.posusa.com/clover-pos-promo-code/).

---

## Pros & Cons

PROS:

* Newest hardware in Clover’s lineup
* Android 13, 4 GB RAM, 64 GB storage
* Built-in receipt printer
* 8+ hours of battery per shift
* Wireless charging cradle included
* Built-in LTE, no WiFi required
* Cheapest full device at $749
* 5MP camera scans 1D/2D barcodes

CONS:

* No cash drawer support
* 5.99″ screen limits complex orders
* Processing rate depends on plan tier
* Hardware locked to your processor
* Receipt paper rolls are small
* Needs a charging routine to stay usable

---

## How Much Does Clover Flex Cost?

Clover Flex costs $749 upfront or $40 per month on a 36-month plan. Three software plans are available, and the plan you choose changes your processing rate as well as your monthly fee. Starter runs 2.6% + 10¢ per in-person transaction, Essentials 2.5% + 10¢, and Services Growth 2.3% + 10¢.

| Plan | Bundled (36 mo.) | Buy Hardware Upfront | Processing Rate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Starter** | $40/mo | $749 | 2.6% + 10¢ |
| **Essentials** | $70/mo | $749 + $29.95/mo | 2.5% + 10¢ |
| **Services Growth** | $125/mo | $749 + $84.95/mo | 2.3% + 10¢ |

Notice that Starter carries no monthly software fee at all. The $40 per month is hardware financing, and $40 × 36 comes to $1,440 against a $749 purchase price. Paying for the device upfront saves nearly $700 on that tier alone.

### When the Higher Tiers Pay for Themselves

The rate difference between Starter and Services Growth is 0.3%, which sounds small until you run it against volume. On $20,000 a month in card sales, that’s $60 saved, against $84.95 in additional software cost. On $40,000 a month it’s $120 saved against the same $84.95, so the upgrade starts paying for itself somewhere around $28,000 in monthly card volume. Below that, Starter is cheaper even though the rate is worse.

That math is specific to the plan tiers on this device. For the full software lineup, fees that don’t appear on the price card, and how Clover’s rates compare across processors, see the [Clover POS review](https://www.posusa.com/clover-pos-review/).

Clover states that the pricing on its site is only available through Clover.com. Independent resellers set their own terms, so a quote from a sales office won’t necessarily match the table above.

---

**Compare Clover Flex to other POS systems**

[Compare POS Prices](https://www.posusa.com/compare/)

---

## Clover Flex vs. Flex Pocket: Which One Do You Need?

Get the Flex if you ever need to hand someone a printed receipt. That’s the whole decision. The Flex 4 and the Flex Pocket run identical internals, the same 5.99″ screen, the same processor, the same 4 GB of RAM, and accept the same payment types. The Flex has a built-in thermal printer and the Pocket doesn’t, and that gap costs $50.

| Clover Flex 4 | Clover Flex Pocket |
| --- | --- |
| **Upfront** | $749 | $699 |
| **Financed** | $40/mo | $35/mo |
| **Receipt printer** | Built-in thermal | None |
| **Charging** | Wireless cradle and USB-C | USB-C only |
| **Display** | 5.99″ IPS LCD | 5.99″ IPS LCD |
| **Processor** | Qualcomm quad-core | Qualcomm quad-core |
| **Memory** | 4 GB RAM, 64 GB Flash | 4 GB RAM, 64 GB Flash |
| **Payments** | Chip, tap, swipe | Chip, tap, swipe |

![Clover Flex Pocket handheld POS terminal](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20800%20500'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

Clover Flex Pocket

The charging difference deserves more attention than it gets. The Flex sits in a wireless cradle between uses, so it tops up every time a server sets it down. The Pocket charges over USB-C only, which means someone has to remember to plug it in. In a restaurant, a device that requires a charging habit is a device that dies during dinner service.

**Choose the Flex 4 if** you’re in food service, retail, or anywhere a customer might ask for a paper receipt, or if the device gets passed between staff during a shift.

**Choose the Flex Pocket if** you’re doing mobile services, delivery, or event sales where digital receipts are the norm and slim size actually matters. Field technicians and delivery drivers are the clearest fit.

For most businesses, the $50 is worth spending. Running out of a receipt option in front of a customer who wants one is a worse problem than $50.

---

## Clover Flex Specs

| Spec | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| **Operating system** | Clover-hardened Android 13 (API level 33) |
| **Processor** | Qualcomm 64-bit ARM Cortex-A53 quad-core |
| **Memory** | 4 GB RAM, 64 GB Flash |
| **Display** | 5.99″ IPS LCD, 1440 x 720, capacitive multi-touch |
| **Battery** | At least 8 hours of typical small business use |
| **Camera** | 5MP, 1D/2D barcode scanning |
| **Payments** | EMV chip, EMV contactless, magstripe |
| **Connectivity** | 4G/LTE, WiFi, Bluetooth |
| **Printer** | Internal thermal receipt printer |
| **Charging** | Wireless charging cradle, USB Type-C |
| **Audio** | 3.5mm stereo jack, mic input, mono speaker |

*Source: [Clover Developer Documentation](https://docs.clover.com/dev/docs/clover-devices-tech-specs)*

### Why the Flex Has Better Internals Than the Station Duo

This is the detail that surprises people. The Flex 4 runs Android 13 with 4 GB of RAM and 64 GB of storage. The [Clover Station Duo](https://www.posusa.com/clover-station-duo/), which costs $1,899, runs Android 10 with 2 GB of RAM and 16 GB of storage on a chipset that dates to 2017.

The Flex is simply the newer product. Clover refreshed the handheld line more recently than the countertop stations, so the least expensive full-featured device in the range is also the most current. That has practical consequences: the Flex handles marketplace apps more comfortably, has more storage headroom, and sits on an OS that will stay supported longer.

None of that makes the Flex a replacement for a countertop station. You still can’t run a cash drawer off it, and a 5.99″ screen is cramped for building a complex ticket. But if you were assuming the expensive device must have better hardware inside, that isn’t the case here.

---

## Battery Life and Daily Use

Clover rates the Flex at a minimum of 8 hours for typical small business use, which covers a standard shift. Real-world results move with how you use it: constant LTE, heavy barcode scanning, and steady receipt printing all pull harder than a device that mostly sits idle between transactions.

The wireless cradle is what makes 8 hours workable in practice. Servers set the device down between tables and it charges without anyone thinking about it, so the battery rarely gets close to empty. Businesses that run a Flex through a full double shift usually buy a second cradle rather than a second device, and swap the unit between stations.

Two things worth planning for. Receipt paper rolls on a handheld are small, so a busy Flex goes through them faster than you’d expect and someone needs to carry spares. And in a building with weak WiFi, the device falls back to LTE, which drains the battery noticeably faster than a strong wireless connection.

---

## How Clover Flex Compares to Other Clover Devices

The Flex is the only portable device in Clover’s lineup. Everything else is a countertop unit that stays where you put it. Here’s how the range compares.

| Flex | [Mini](https://www.posusa.com/clover-mini/) | Station Solo | [Station Duo](https://www.posusa.com/clover-station-duo/) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Upfront** | $749 | $849 | $1,799 | $1,899 |
| **Financed** | $40/mo | $45/mo | $174/mo | $180/mo |
| **Screen** | 5.99″ | 8″ | 14″ | 14″ + 8″ |
| **Portable** | Yes | No | No | No |
| **Receipt printer** | Built in | Built in | Built in | Built in |
| **Cash drawer** | No | Optional add-on | Included | Included |
| **Best for** | Tableside, curbside, mobile | Small counter, tight space | Back office, low interaction | Counter service, high volume |

A common setup for small restaurants is a Mini on the counter and a Flex for the floor, which comes to $1,598 and costs less than a single Station Duo. That gives you a fixed position and a mobile one instead of one large station.

---

## Clover Flex vs. Square Terminal

Square Terminal is the closest competitor: a handheld with a built-in receipt printer aimed at the same tableside use cases. It costs $299 against the Flex’s $749, which is a real gap. The catch is connectivity. Square Terminal runs on WiFi, or Ethernet with a separately sold Hub accessory. It has no cellular radio at all. The Clover Flex has 4G/LTE built in.

| Clover Flex | [Square Terminal](https://www.posusa.com/square-terminal-review/) |
| --- | --- |
| **Hardware cost** | $749 | $299 |
| **Screen** | 5.99″ | 5.5″ |
| **Receipt printer** | Built in | Built in |
| **Cellular (LTE)** | Yes, built in | No |
| **Connectivity** | 4G/LTE, WiFi, Bluetooth | WiFi, Ethernet via optional Hub |
| **Contract** | 36 months if financed | None |
| **Monthly software** | $0–$84.95 | $0 on the free plan |
| **Processing** | 2.3%–2.6% + 10¢ | 2.6% + 15¢ |
| **Choose your processor** | No | No |

That difference decides the comparison for a lot of businesses. A [food truck](https://www.posusa.com/food-truck-pos-systems/), a farmers market booth, a mobile groomer, a repair tech at a customer’s house, a caterer at an event venue: none of those can count on WiFi, and Square Terminal has no answer for it. If payment happens away from a building you control, the Flex is the only one of the two that works.

Inside four walls with reliable WiFi, the calculation flips. Square Terminal does the same job for $450 less with no contract, and Square’s flat 2.6% + 15¢ is close enough to Clover’s rates that the hardware savings dominate for most small operations.

**Pick the Clover Flex if** you need cellular connectivity, you want the app marketplace, or you’re already running other Clover devices.

**Pick Square Terminal if** your WiFi is solid, you want no contract, and you’d rather put the $450 difference somewhere else. Our [Square POS review](https://www.posusa.com/square-pos-review/) covers the full platform.

---

## Who Should Buy the Clover Flex?

### ✅ Good fit for

* **Full-service restaurants** running tableside ordering and payment, where turning tables faster is worth more than the device costs
* **Coffee shops and quick-service spots** that need to bust lines during a rush without adding a permanent register
* **Curbside and takeout operations** where payment happens at a car window rather than a counter
* **Mobile service businesses** like landscapers, mobile groomers, and repair techs who collect payment at the job site
* **[Food trucks](https://www.posusa.com/food-truck-pos-systems/), farmers market vendors, and pop-ups** that need LTE connectivity and a printed receipt without any fixed infrastructure
* **Salons and barber shops** where checkout happens at the chair instead of a front desk

If you’re comparing options across brands, our roundup of [POS systems for small business](https://www.posusa.com/small-business-pos-systems/) covers the alternatives in this range.

### ❌ Not ideal for

* **Businesses that need a cash drawer.** The Flex can’t drive one. The [Clover Mini](https://www.posusa.com/clover-mini/) takes an optional drawer, and the Stations include one.
* **High-volume counter service** with a fixed checkout point, where the [Station Duo](https://www.posusa.com/clover-station-duo/) and its customer-facing screen move a line faster
* **Complex ticket building.** A 5.99″ screen gets tight when orders have many modifiers and course timing.
* **Anyone likely to switch processors,** since Clover hardware doesn’t transfer between them
* **Businesses that want no contract at all,** where Square Terminal is the simpler path

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How much does Clover Flex cost?

Clover Flex costs $749 upfront or $40 per month on a 36-month plan. Three software tiers are available: Starter at $749 with no monthly fee, Essentials at $749 plus $29.95 per month, and Services Growth at $749 plus $84.95 per month. Processing runs 2.6% + 10¢ on Starter, 2.5% + 10¢ on Essentials, and 2.3% + 10¢ on Services Growth.

### What's the difference between Clover Flex and Flex Pocket?

The Clover Flex has a built-in thermal receipt printer and a wireless charging cradle. The Flex Pocket has neither and charges over USB-C only. Everything else is the same: both run Android 13 on a Qualcomm quad-core processor with 4 GB of RAM, both have a 5.99″ screen, and both accept chip, tap, and swipe payments. Flex costs $749, Flex Pocket costs $699.

### How long does the Clover Flex battery last?

Clover rates the Flex at a minimum of 8 hours for typical small business use, enough for a standard shift. Heavy LTE use, constant barcode scanning, and frequent receipt printing shorten that. The included wireless charging cradle keeps the device topped up between transactions, which is how most businesses get through a full day without a swap.

### Does the Clover Flex print receipts?

Yes. The Clover Flex has an internal thermal receipt printer built into the device, so no separate printer is needed. The Flex Pocket does not have one and relies on emailed or texted receipts. This is the main difference between the two models.

### Can Clover Flex work with a cash drawer?

No. The Flex is a handheld device with no cash drawer connection. If you take cash regularly and need a drawer that opens on a sale, look at the [Clover Mini](https://www.posusa.com/clover-mini/), which takes a cash drawer as an optional add-on, or a Station, which includes one.

### Does Clover Flex work without WiFi?

Yes. The Flex has built-in 4G/LTE alongside WiFi and Bluetooth, so it can process payments anywhere with cell coverage. That makes it workable for food trucks, farmers markets, curbside pickup, and mobile service calls. It’s also the main hardware difference against Square Terminal, which has no cellular radio and needs WiFi or a wired Hub accessory. Running on LTE drains the Flex battery faster than a strong WiFi connection.

### Is Clover Flex better than Clover Station Duo?

It depends on where payment happens. The Flex is portable and has newer internals: Android 13, 4 GB of RAM, and 64 GB of storage against the Station Duo’s Android 10, 2 GB, and 16 GB. The Duo has a 14″ merchant screen, an 8″ customer display, and an included cash drawer, which the Flex can’t match for fixed counter service. Buy the Flex for mobility, the Duo for a busy fixed checkout.

### Does the $450 Clover promo apply to the Flex?

Yes. Both the Clover Flex and Flex Pocket are eligible devices for Clover’s $450 statement credit, along with the Mini, Station Solo, and Station Duo. New merchants who qualify and meet the activation requirements get the credit applied automatically. See our [Clover promo details](https://www.posusa.com/clover-pos-promo-code/) for current terms.

### Can I use a Clover Flex with a different payment processor?

No. Clover hardware is provisioned for Fiserv or your reseller’s processor and cannot be reprogrammed for another one. Switching processors means buying new hardware, which is also why secondhand Clover devices usually can’t be activated by a new owner.

### Can Clover Flex scan barcodes?

Yes. The Flex has a 5MP integrated camera that scans 1D and 2D barcodes using Zebra scan decoding software. That covers retail inventory lookups, QR codes, and product scanning without a separate accessory.

---

## Our Verdict

The Clover Flex is the best value in Clover’s hardware range, and it isn’t close. At $749 you get the newest internals Clover ships, a built-in receipt printer, LTE, barcode scanning, and a wireless charging cradle in a device that goes wherever the transaction happens. For restaurants running tableside service or any business collecting payment away from a counter, it does the job well.

The limits are the ones you’d expect from a handheld. No cash drawer, and a 5.99″ screen that gets cramped when a ticket has a lot of modifiers. Neither is a flaw so much as a definition of what the device is for. Where it gets interesting is against the countertop stations, since the Flex runs Android 13 with 4 GB of RAM while the $1,899 Station Duo runs Android 10 with 2 GB. Spending more on Clover hardware does not get you newer hardware.

If you take cash regularly or run a high-volume fixed counter, pair the Flex with a Mini or a Station rather than trying to make it the whole system. And if you finance, know that $40 per month for 36 months comes to $1,440 on a $749 device. Buying outright is the better deal on every tier.

**Expert Rating:** ⭐ **9.0/10** – The most modern hardware Clover makes at the lowest price in the lineup, with a printer and LTE built in. The score covers the device. Clover’s contract terms, software costs, and support reputation are evaluated in our [Clover POS review](https://www.posusa.com/clover-pos-review/).

## Clover Flex Handheld POS Terminal - Summary

The Clover Flex is a handheld POS terminal (model Flex 4, as of July 2026) with a 5.99" touchscreen, built-in thermal receipt printer, and 8+ hours of battery life. It costs **$749 upfront** or **$40/month on a 36-month plan** ($1,440 total if financed).

**Key Hardware Specs:** Android 13, Qualcomm quad-core processor, 4GB RAM, 64GB storage, 5MP camera (1D/2D barcode scanning), EMV chip/tap/swipe, built-in 4G/LTE, WiFi, Bluetooth, wireless charging cradle and USB-C.

**Software Plans & Processing Rates:**
- **Starter:** $749 (no monthly fee) – 2.6% + 10¢ per transaction
- **Essentials:** $749 + $29.95/mo – 2.5% + 10¢
- **Services Growth:** $749 + $84.95/mo – 2.3% + 10¢

The Services Growth tier pays for itself around $28,000/month in card volume.

**Clover Flex vs. Flex Pocket:** The only difference is the Flex has a built-in printer and wireless charging cradle ($749), while the Pocket does not ($699). Both have identical internals.

**Clover Flex vs. Square Terminal:** Square Terminal costs $299 but has no cellular radio (WiFi/Ethernet only). The Flex has built-in LTE, making it better for food trucks, markets, and mobile businesses. Inside reliable WiFi, Square Terminal is the better value.

**Notable:** The Flex 4 has newer internals than the $1,899 Station Duo (Android 13 vs. Android 10, 4GB vs. 2GB RAM). It's the cheapest full-featured device in Clover's lineup but is also the most modern.

**Limitations:** No cash drawer support, 5.99" screen is cramped for complex orders, hardware locked to processor, receipt paper rolls are small.

**Best For:** Full-service restaurants, coffee shops, food trucks, curbside/takeout, mobile service businesses, salons. Not ideal for high-volume fixed counter service or businesses needing cash drawers.

**Expert Rating: 9.0/10** – Best value in Clover's hardware range. A limited-time $450 Clover promo (statement credit) applies to both Flex and Flex Pocket for eligible new merchants.

"Free" POS systems offset their $0 software cost with higher processing rates, so you still pay, just differently.

## How Much Does a POS System Cost for a Restaurant?

How much is a POS system for a restaurant? The short answer: $1,000 to $10,000+ in total first-year restaurant point of sale systems cost (hardware, software, and setup, before processing fees), with most single-location restaurants paying $3,000 to $5,000. But the real restaurant POS cost depends on three layers, and most vendors only talk about one of them. Here is what you actually pay:

1. **Hardware**: one-time purchase or lease (terminals, readers, kitchen displays)

2. **Software**: monthly subscription fee for the POS application

3. **Processing fees**: a percentage of every card transaction, charged per swipe or tap

Each layer varies by vendor. Some offer free software but charge higher processing rates. Others sell cheap hardware but lock you into multi-year contracts. To compare POS systems honestly, you need to look at all three layers together.

### Hardware Costs

POS hardware ranges from a $59 card reader to a $1,899 full station with a customer-facing display. Here is what each piece costs across major vendors in 2026:

| Hardware | Cost Range | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mobile card reader | $59-$199 | Square Reader $59, Toast Go reader $100+ |
| Handheld POS | $399-$627 | Toast Go 2 $627 (source: Toast pricing page), Square Terminal $299-$399 |
| Countertop terminal | $299-$849 | Square Terminal $299, Toast countertop terminal $799+ (source: Toast hardware page) |
| Full station (terminal + stand + printer + drawer) | $799-$1,899 | Toast Starter Kit $799+, Square Register $799, Clover Station Duo $1,799 (source: Clover.com) |
| Kitchen Display System (KDS) | $499-$899 + $25-$35/mo | Toast KDS $499+, Square KDS $20/mo per device (source: Square pricing) |
| Typical single-terminal setup | $600-$2,000 | Includes terminal, receipt printer, cash drawer |
| Full multi-terminal setup (2-3 stations) | $2,000-$5,000+ | Full-service restaurant with KDS and handhelds |

**Key detail:** Toast and Clover sell proprietary hardware. If you leave Toast, those terminals become paperweights. Square and SpotOn use standard iPads or Android tablets, so you keep the hardware if you switch.

### Software Subscription

Monthly software costs range from free to $399, with most restaurant-focused plans landing between $49 and $189 per month:

| Monthly Range | Examples |
| --- | --- |
| $0/month | Square for Restaurants Free (source: squareup.com/us/en/software/restaurant), Toast Starter (source: pos.toasttab.com/pricing), SpotOn Quick Start |
| $49-$69/mo | Square for Restaurants Plus $60/mo (source: squareup.com), Toast POS $69/mo (source: Toast pricing), TouchBistro $69/mo (source: touchbistro.com/pricing) |
| $89-$189/mo | Clover Dining $89.95-$129.85/mo (source: clover.com/pricing), Lightspeed Restaurant Essential $189/mo (source: lightspeedhq.com/pos/restaurant/pricing) |
| $99-$399/mo | Revel $99/terminal/mo (source: revelsystems.com), Lightspeed Premium $399/mo (source: Lightspeed pricing page) |

Free plans from Square, Toast, and SpotOn are genuine, you get a working POS with no monthly charge. The tradeoff is higher processing rates and fewer features. More on that below.

### Processing Fees (the Real Cost)

Processing fees are the largest ongoing expense for most restaurants. Here is what each major POS charges per in-person transaction in 2026:

| POS System | In-Person Rate | Online/Keyed Rate | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Toast (Starter) | 2.99% + $0.15 | 3.09% + $0.15 | pos.toasttab.com/pricing |
| Toast (paid plans) | 2.49% + $0.15 (custom rates available) | 3.09% + $0.15 | pos.toasttab.com/pricing |
| Square | 2.6% + $0.10 | 2.9% + $0.30 | squareup.com/us/en/payments/processing-fees |
| Clover (Fiserv) | 2.3% + $0.10 | 3.5% + $0.10 | clover.com/pricing |
| Lightspeed | 2.6% + $0.10 | 2.9% + $0.30 | lightspeedhq.com/pos/restaurant/pricing |
| SpotOn (free plan) | 2.79% + $0.15 | 2.79% + $0.15 | spoton.com/pricing |
| SpotOn (paid plan) | 1.99% + $0.25 | 1.99% + $0.25 | spoton.com/pricing |
| Revel | Custom (negotiated) | Custom | revelsystems.com |
| TouchBistro | Custom (third-party processor) | Custom | touchbistro.com |

*Rates verified against each vendor's published pricing page as of July 2026. Always confirm current rates with the vendor before signing.*

**The math matters.** On $50,000 per month in card sales, the difference between 2.3% and 2.79% is $245 per month, or $2,940 per year. That is often more than the software subscription itself.

### First-Year Total Restaurant POS System Cost

How much does a restaurant POS system cost in total? Combining hardware, software, and processing fees for a restaurant doing $50,000 per month in card sales:

| Setup Level | Hardware | Software (12 mo) | Processing (12 mo) | First-Year Total |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Budget (free plan + basic terminal) | $300-$600 | $0 | $15,000-$17,000 | ~$15,500-$17,500 |
| Mid-range (paid plan + full station) | $800-$1,500 | $600-$830 | $13,800-$15,600 | ~$15,200-$17,900 |
| Full-service (multi-terminal + KDS) | $2,000-$5,000 | $1,200-$4,800 | $13,800-$15,600 | ~$17,000-$25,400 |

Notice that processing fees dominate every scenario. The "free" POS often costs nearly the same as the paid one because higher processing rates eat the software savings. Seen [measured against 2026 restaurant profit margin benchmarks](/blog/restaurant-profit-margin-benchmarks-2026), those processing points are the difference between a thin profit and none.

## Top 7 Restaurant POS Systems Compared (2026 Pricing)

### 1. Toast POS Pricing

Toast POS pricing starts at $0 per month on the Starter plan and $69 per month on the standard POS plan in 2026, with in-person processing at 2.49% + $0.15 on paid plans and 2.99% + $0.15 on Starter. Here is the full picture, with more detail in the cost tables above.

**Software:** $0/mo (Starter), $69/mo (POS), custom pricing for higher tiers (source: pos.toasttab.com/pricing)

**Processing:** 2.49% + $0.15 in-person, 3.09% + $0.15 online. On Starter plan: 2.99% + $0.15 in-person (source: Toast pricing page)

**Contract:** Month-to-month on Starter. 2-year commitment on paid plans. Early termination fees apply.

**Hardware:** Proprietary. Toast hardware only works with Toast software, and you cannot take it with you if you switch.

**Best for:** Full-service restaurants that want deep kitchen integration, table management, and restaurant-specific features.

Toast is the most popular restaurant-specific POS in the U.S., with over 120,000 restaurant locations (source: Toast 2025 annual report). Its strength is the all-in-one ecosystem: POS, online ordering, payroll, kitchen displays, and marketing all work together. The downside is lock-in. Toast hardware is proprietary, paid plans require a 2-year contract, and adding features like online ordering ($75/mo), loyalty, or marketing pushes the real monthly cost well above the $69 base. Most Toast restaurants report paying $150 to $500 per month once they add the modules they need (source: Toast user reviews on G2 and Capterra, 2025-2026).

### 2. Square for Restaurants Pricing

Square for Restaurants pricing starts at $0 per month on the Free plan, with paid plans at $60 per month (Plus) and $153 per month (Premium) in 2026, and in-person processing at 2.6% + $0.10.

**Software:** $0/mo (Free), $60/mo (Plus), $153/mo (Premium) (source: squareup.com/us/en/software/restaurant)

**Processing:** 2.6% + $0.10 in-person, 2.9% + $0.30 online (source: squareup.com/us/en/payments/processing-fees)

**Contract:** None. Month-to-month, cancel any time.

**Hardware:** Uses iPads and Square's own readers/terminals. You keep the hardware if you leave.

**Best for:** Quick-service restaurants, food trucks, counter-service cafes, and startups that need flexibility.

Square is the easiest POS to set up and the hardest to get locked into. There are no contracts, no proprietary hardware requirements, and a free plan that is genuinely useful for small operations. The free plan includes order management, menu management, and basic reporting. The Plus plan adds floor plans, coursing, and seat management for $60 per month. Processing rates are higher than Clover but lower than Toast's free plan. Square also has the broadest ecosystem of any POS, with payroll, banking, invoicing, and marketing tools that all connect.

### 3. Clover

Clover restaurant POS pricing starts at $89.95 per month for the Dining Starter plan in 2026, with the lowest published flat processing rate of any major POS at 2.3% + $0.10 in person via Fiserv.

**Software:** $89.95/mo (Dining Starter), $109.90/mo (Dining Standard), $129.85/mo (Dining Advanced), for restaurant-specific plans (source: clover.com/pricing)

**Processing:** 2.3% + $0.10 in-person (with Fiserv), 3.5% + $0.10 keyed-in (source: clover.com/pricing)

**Contract:** 36-to-48-month contracts through most resellers. Some month-to-month options available directly from Clover/Fiserv.

**Hardware:** Proprietary Clover devices. Clover Station Duo $1,799, Clover Mini $799, Clover Flex $599 (source: clover.com/hardware)

**Best for:** Restaurants that want the lowest flat-rate processing fees and are comfortable with longer contracts.

Clover has the lowest published flat processing rate at 2.3% + $0.10, which saves real money at higher volumes. The catch is the reseller model. Clover is sold through hundreds of independent resellers, and pricing, contract terms, and support quality vary widely. Some resellers mark up hardware 50% or more. Others offer good deals but lock you into 48-month leases. Always buy directly from Clover.com or from a Fiserv-authorized dealer to get published pricing. Also note: Clover hardware is proprietary, so switching POS means buying new hardware.

### 4. Lightspeed Restaurant Pricing

Lightspeed Restaurant pricing starts at $69 per month for the Starter plan in 2026, rising to $189 per month (Essential) and $399 per month (Premium) billed annually, with in-person processing at 2.6% + $0.10.

**Software:** $69/mo (Starter), $189/mo (Essential), $399/mo (Premium), billed annually (source: lightspeedhq.com/pos/restaurant/pricing)

**Processing:** 2.6% + $0.10 in-person (source: Lightspeed pricing page)

**Contract:** Annual billing required for published rates. Month-to-month available at higher prices.

**Hardware:** iPad-based. Uses standard iPads with Lightspeed's app.

**Best for:** Restaurants with complex menus, large wine lists, multi-location inventory needs, and high-volume bars.

Lightspeed stands out for its inventory management and menu flexibility. If you run a restaurant with hundreds of SKUs, seasonal menus, or complex modifiers, Lightspeed handles that better than Square or Toast. Online ordering is included in the Essential and Premium plans with no commission. The downside is cost: the Essential plan at $189 per month is more expensive than most competitors, and the Starter plan is limited. Lightspeed is best for mid-to-large restaurants that can justify the higher price with the advanced features.

### 5. SpotOn

SpotOn pricing starts at $0 per month on the Quick Start plan and $55 per month on paid restaurant plans in 2026, with processing at 2.79% + $0.15 on the free plan and 1.99% + $0.25 on paid plans.

**Software:** $0/mo (Quick Start), $55/mo (Counter), $55+/mo (Restaurant) (source: spoton.com/restaurant-pos)

**Processing:** 2.79% + $0.15 on free plan, 1.99% + $0.25 on paid plans (source: spoton.com/pricing)

**Contract:** No long-term contracts. Month-to-month.

**Hardware:** Proprietary SpotOn terminals, but also supports third-party hardware.

**Best for:** Restaurants that want commission-free online ordering built into their POS without paying extra.

SpotOn is the strongest value proposition for restaurants that need both POS and online ordering. The paid plan at $55 per month includes commission-free online ordering, a branded ordering website, and a lower processing rate (1.99% + $0.25) that can save hundreds per month compared to Square or Toast. No contracts, and the Quick Start free plan is a legitimate option for small operations. The 1.99% rate on paid plans is one of the lowest in the market, though the $0.25 per-transaction flat fee is higher than competitors, which means the savings are largest for restaurants with higher average ticket sizes.

### 6. Revel Systems

**Software:** $99/terminal/mo, 2-terminal minimum ($198/mo minimum) (source: revelsystems.com/pricing)

**Processing:** Custom, negotiated per account. Revel uses its own payment processing or approved third-party processors.

**Contract:** 3-year contract required (source: Revel terms of service).

**Hardware:** iPad-based with proprietary peripherals.

**Best for:** Multi-location restaurants and enterprise operations that need advanced reporting, open API access, and custom integrations.

Revel is an enterprise-grade POS that comes with enterprise-grade pricing and commitments. The 2-terminal minimum and 3-year contract make it a poor fit for single-location restaurants just getting started. Where Revel shines is in multi-location management, advanced reporting, and API access for custom integrations. If you run 3+ locations and need centralized control with detailed analytics, Revel delivers. For everyone else, the cost and commitment are hard to justify when Toast or SpotOn offer similar features with more flexible terms.

### 7. TouchBistro Pricing

TouchBistro pricing starts at $69 per month for the base POS in 2026, with add-ons (online ordering $50/mo, reservations $229/mo, loyalty $99/mo, marketing $99/mo) that can raise the total to $546 per month.

**Software:** $69/mo base (source: touchbistro.com/pricing). Add-ons: online ordering $50/mo, reservations $229/mo, loyalty $99/mo, marketing $99/mo.

**Processing:** TouchBistro partners with Chase for payment processing. Rates are custom and negotiated. TouchBistro does not publish processing rates.

**Contract:** Multi-year contracts are standard. Early termination fees apply (source: TouchBistro terms).

**Hardware:** iPad-only. Runs on standard Apple iPads.

**Best for:** Sit-down restaurants that need strong table management and floor plan features.

TouchBistro's base POS at $69 per month is competitive, and its table management and floor plan features are among the best in the market. The problem is the add-on pricing. If you need online ordering ($50/mo), reservations ($229/mo), loyalty ($99/mo), and marketing ($99/mo), you are paying $546 per month. That is more than Lightspeed Premium. TouchBistro makes sense if you only need the core POS with table management and will use a separate solution for online ordering and marketing.

---

## Which Restaurant Point of Sale Systems Have No Monthly Fee?

Four POS systems offer a genuine $0 per month plan for restaurants:

| POS | Free Plan Name | Processing Rate | Limitations |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Square for Restaurants | Free | 2.6% + $0.10 | No floor plans, no coursing, limited reporting |
| Toast | Starter | 2.99% + $0.15 | Limited features, higher processing rate |
| SpotOn | Quick Start | 2.79% + $0.15 | Basic features, no online ordering |
| Aldelo Express | Free (with Aldelo Pay) | 2.5% + varies | Must use Aldelo Pay for processing |

**The tradeoff is real.** On $30,000 per month in card sales, the difference between a free plan at 2.99% and a paid plan at 2.49% is $150 per month in extra processing fees. That is $1,800 per year. If the paid plan costs $69 per month ($828/year), you save $972 per year by switching to the paid plan. Free is not always cheaper.

The breakeven point is roughly $15,000 to $20,000 per month in card volume. Below that, the free plan usually wins. Above that, a paid plan with lower processing rates costs less in total.

---

## Square vs Toast vs Clover: Head-to-Head

These three are the most-compared restaurant POS systems. Here is how they stack up side by side:

| Feature | Square | Toast | Clover |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Primary focus | General POS with restaurant features | Restaurant-specific | General POS with restaurant plans |
| Free plan | Yes ($0/mo) | Yes ($0/mo Starter) | No (starts at $89.95/mo) |
| Paid plan | $60/mo (Plus) | $69/mo (POS) | $89.95-$129.85/mo |
| In-person processing | 2.6% + $0.10 | 2.49% + $0.15 | 2.3% + $0.10 |
| Online processing | 2.9% + $0.30 | 3.09% + $0.15 | 3.5% + $0.10 |
| Hardware | iPad + Square devices (portable) | Proprietary Toast devices (locked) | Proprietary Clover devices (locked) |
| Contracts | No contracts | 2-year on paid plans | 36-48 months via resellers |
| Online ordering | Square Online (free-$72/mo) | Toast add-on ($75/mo) | Clover Online Ordering ($50/mo add-on) |
| Choose your processor | No (Square only) | No (Toast only) | Yes (Fiserv or approved third-party) |
| Best for | QSR, food trucks, budget startups | Full-service, multi-location | High-volume wanting lowest rate |

**Bottom line:** Square for flexibility and zero commitment. Toast for the deepest restaurant feature set if you can handle the contract and proprietary hardware. Clover for the lowest processing rates if you buy through a reputable dealer and are comfortable with a multi-year contract.

---

## What POS Do Big Chains Use?

If you are curious what the big names run:

* **McDonald's**: NP6 (proprietary system developed in-house, not commercially available)
* **Chick-fil-A**: NCR Aloha (heavily customized version, not available in that configuration to independents)
* **Starbucks**: Oracle MICROS Simphony (enterprise POS, licensed for large chains)
* **Taco Bell / KFC / Pizza Hut**: Byte by Yum! (formerly Poseidon, built by Yum Brands' internal tech division)
* **Subway**: Oracle MICROS (custom configuration)

The key takeaway: chains use proprietary or heavily customized enterprise systems that are either not sold to independents or cost six figures to implement. None of these are realistic options for a single-location or small-chain restaurant. The systems reviewed earlier in this guide (Toast, Square, Clover, SpotOn, Lightspeed, Revel, TouchBistro) are the practical choices for independent operators.

---

## The Hidden Costs Nobody Tells You About

Beyond the published prices, several costs catch restaurant owners off guard:

**PCI compliance fees:** Most processors charge $9.95 to $10 per month for PCI compliance (source: Merchant Maverick processor fee survey, 2025). Some charge a non-compliance fee of $19.95 to $29.95 per month if you do not complete your annual PCI self-assessment questionnaire.

**Average unexpected cost:** According to a 2025 Hospitality Technology survey, restaurant operators reported an average of $2,400 per year in unexpected POS-related costs per location, including add-on fees, compliance charges, and support costs that were not clearly disclosed during the sales process.

**Proprietary hardware lock-in:** Toast and Clover hardware only works with their software. If you leave, you buy new hardware. On a full station setup, that is $1,500 to $3,000 in sunk cost. Square, SpotOn, and Lightspeed use standard iPads or Android devices that work with any POS.

**Add-on creep:** Toast's base plan is $69 per month, but most restaurants add online ordering ($75/mo), loyalty ($50/mo), marketing ($75/mo), payroll ($40+/mo), and other modules. Real-world spend on Toast commonly reaches $150 to $500 per month (source: G2 and Capterra user reviews, 2025-2026). The same pattern applies to TouchBistro, where the base $69 plan can grow to $500+ with all add-ons.

**Reseller pricing variation:** Clover's reseller model means the price you pay depends on who you buy from. Some resellers offer competitive pricing. Others mark up hardware 50-100% or add hidden monthly fees that are not on Clover's published pricing. Always compare reseller quotes against clover.com direct pricing.

**Early termination fees:** Breaking a POS contract early can cost $295 to $10,000+ depending on the vendor and remaining contract length. Toast's early termination fee is based on remaining contract value. Revel's 3-year contract includes substantial ETF provisions. Square and SpotOn have no contracts, so there is nothing to terminate.

---

## How POS Connects to Online Ordering

Your POS and your online ordering system need to talk to each other. Orders placed online should flow directly into your kitchen without anyone re-entering them by hand. There are three models for how this works:

**Built-in online ordering:** Some POS systems include online ordering as a native feature. Square, SpotOn, and Lightspeed all offer built-in or included online ordering. Orders sync automatically because they run on the same platform. This is the simplest option.

**Add-on online ordering:** Toast charges $75 per month to add online ordering to your POS (source: Toast pricing page). Clover charges $50 per month for its online ordering module. These integrate tightly because they are built by the same company, but they cost extra.

**Third-party middleware:** If your POS does not have good built-in online ordering, or if you want to connect to multiple delivery platforms, middleware services like Chowly or Deliverect ($50 to $200 per month) bridge the gap. They take orders from third-party platforms and push them into your POS. This works, but adds another monthly cost and another vendor to manage.

**The bigger question:** Whether your orders come through built-in POS ordering or a separate online ordering system, the critical issue is whether you are paying 15-30% commission on delivery orders through marketplace apps. A POS with commission-free online ordering, or a separate [commission-free ordering platform](/online-ordering-system), can save you thousands per month compared to relying on DoorDash or Uber Eats for your online orders. # Restaurant POS System Cost 2026: Comprehensive Guide

## Overview
A US restaurant POS system costs **$1,000 to $10,000+** in year-one hardware, software, and setup costs, with **$3,000 to $5,000 typical** for a single-location setup. The biggest ongoing cost is processing fees — on $50,000 monthly card volume, processing alone runs **$12,000 to $18,000 per year**.

## Three Cost Layers

1. **Hardware (one-time):** $600–$2,000 for a single terminal; $2,000–$5,000+ for multi-terminal setups. Range: $59 card reader to $1,899 full station.
2. **Software (monthly):** $0–$399/month. Most restaurant plans: $49–$189/month.
3. **Processing fees (variable):** The largest ongoing expense. Rates range from 1.99% to 2.99% + per-transaction fees.

## Top 7 POS Systems Compared (2026 Pricing)

| POS | Software | In-Person Processing | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Toast** | $0/mo (Starter), $69/mo (POS) | 2.49%+$0.15 (paid), 2.99%+$0.15 (free) | 2-year on paid plans; proprietary hardware |
| **Square** | $0/mo (Free), $60/mo (Plus) | 2.6%+$0.10 | No contracts; iPad-based |
| **Clover** | $89.95–$129.85/mo | 2.3%+$0.10 (lowest flat rate) | 36–48 month contracts; proprietary hardware |
| **Lightspeed** | $69–$399/mo | 2.6%+$0.10 | Annual billing; iPad-based |
| **SpotOn** | $0/mo (Quick Start), $55/mo (paid) | 2.79%+$0.15 (free), 1.99%+$0.25 (paid) | No contracts |
| **Revel** | $99/terminal/mo (2-terminal min) | Custom/negotiated | 3-year contract |
| **TouchBistro** | $69/mo base (add-ons up to $546/mo) | Custom (Chase) | Multi-year contracts |

## Key Insights

- **"Free" POS ≠ cheaper:** Free plans offset $0 software with 0.4–0.6 points higher processing. Breakeven is ~$15K–$20K/month in card volume. Above that, paid plans save money.
- **Processing fees dominate:** On $50K/month, the difference between 2.3% and 2.79% is $245/month ($2,940/year).
- **Hidden costs:** PCI compliance ($10/mo), proprietary hardware lock-in ($1,500–$3,000 sunk cost), add-on creep (Toast real-world: $150–$500/mo), early termination fees ($295–$10,000+), and average $2,400/year in unexpected POS costs.
- **Big chains** use proprietary enterprise systems (Oracle MICROS, NCR Aloha) not available to independents.
- **Online ordering integration:** Built-in (Square, SpotOn, Lightspeed), add-on (Toast $75/mo, Clover $50/mo), or third-party middleware (Chowly/Deliverect $50–$200/mo). Commission-free ordering platforms can save thousands vs. DoorDash/Uber Eats.

<webpage_content>
Technology

# Clover vs Square for Restaurants: Which Should You Pick in 2026?

2026-06-09• Tom Lawton

**Quick answer:** Square is the lower-cost way into a restaurant POS — a free entry plan, transparent self-serve pricing, and hardware from $59. Clover charges more for software but carries lower card-present processing rates on its restaurant plans (2.3% + 10¢ as reported, versus Square's 2.6% + 15¢ on its free tier) and includes online ordering with its restaurant software. The structural difference most comparisons skip: Square sells one way, direct; Clover is sold direct, through banks, and through resellers, so your actual price and contract depend on where you buy. Chowly integrates with both, which is why this comparison has no horse in the race.

Most "Clover vs. Square" comparisons are written for every small business at once — boutiques, salons, coffee carts, dog groomers. That framing doesn't help a restaurant operator weighing a kitchen display system against a printer, or comparing processing rates at a $30 average ticket and a Friday-night rush. This guide compares the two strictly through a restaurant lens: software pricing, processing fees with worked math, hardware, kitchen and table features, and the buying process itself.

One housekeeping note up front: all pricing below is as of June 2026 and can change. Square figures come straight from [Square's published pricing](https://squareup.com/us/en/pricing). Clover sells through multiple channels and quotes bundle pricing, so Clover figures are triangulated from current third-party trackers — [Tech.co's Clover pricing breakdown](https://tech.co/pos-system/clover-pos-pricing) (December 2025) and [NerdWallet's Clover vs. Square review](https://www.nerdwallet.com/business/software/learn/clover-vs-square) (2026) — and cross-checked against [Square's own comparison page](https://squareup.com/us/en/compare/square-vs-clover). Confirm against [Clover's restaurant pricing page](https://www.clover.com/pricing/restaurant) and your actual quote before you sign anything.

## Square vs. Clover at a Glance

| Dimension | Square | Clover (as reported, June 2026) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entry software price | $0/mo (Square Free) | ~$89.95/mo (restaurant Starter plans) |
| Mid/top software | Plus $49/mo per location; Premium $149/mo per location | FSR Standard ~$109.90/mo; FSR Advanced ~$129.85/mo |
| Card-present rate | 2.6% + 15¢ (Free), 2.5% + 15¢ (Plus), 2.4% + 15¢ (Premium) | 2.3% + 10¢ on restaurant plans |
| Online rate | 3.3% + 30¢ (Free), 2.9% + 30¢ (Plus/Premium) | 3.5% + 10¢ keyed/card-not-present |
| Cheapest hardware | Magstripe reader (first one free); Reader $59 | Clover Go $199 |
| Flagship hardware | Square Register $899 | Station Duo $1,899 |
| Handheld | Square Handheld $399 | Clover Flex from around $649 (sources differ) |
| KDS | $20–$30/device/mo app (Plus/Premium only) | Included in higher restaurant bundles |
| Online ordering | Square Online, free tier + processing | Included with restaurant plans |
| Contract | None; month to month | Varies by seller; resellers often 36–48 months |
| Works with Chowly | [Yes — POS-native](/pos/chowly-for-square/) | [Yes — POS-native](/pos/chowly-for-clover/) |

Sources: squareup.com pricing and comparison pages; Tech.co (Dec 2025); NerdWallet (2026); Merchant Maverick (Nov 2025). Clover figures as reported — verify with Clover or your reseller.

## Software Pricing: What Each Plan Actually Costs

**Square** publishes three tiers, all self-serve, all month to month:

* **Square Free** — $0/mo. Full POS, payments, basic reporting. No KDS app access.
* **Square Plus** — $49/mo per location. Adds the restaurant feature set: coursing, advanced reporting, KDS access ($30/device/mo), and more. Comes with a 30-day free trial.
* **Square Premium** — $149/mo per location. Lower processing rates, cheaper per-device KDS ($20/device/mo), and priority support. Square also offers custom pricing if you process more than $250K a year.

**Clover** structures its restaurant software by format — quick-service (QSR) and full-service (FSR) — with Starter, Standard, and Advanced tiers. As reported by Tech.co (December 2025), with hardware purchased upfront, software runs about **$89.95/mo for Starter plans** up to **$109.90/mo (QSR Advanced)** and **$129.85/mo (FSR Advanced)**. Those figures independently match what Square lists on its own Clover comparison page, which is decent triangulation, but Clover's site quotes bundles, so treat these as reported figures.

Clover also sells hardware-and-software bundles paid over 36 months — roughly **$135/mo for a QSR Starter bundle up to about $354/mo for FSR Advanced**, which includes a Station Duo and a Flex handheld, per Tech.co. The bundle route lowers your upfront cash but commits you for three years, which matters more than it sounds (more on that in the buying-process section).

**Restaurant takeaway:** Square lets you start at literally $0 in software and upgrade when the volume justifies it. Clover starts near $90/mo but packs more restaurant functionality into the base restaurant plans. Neither approach is wrong — they're priced for different buyers.

## Processing Fees: Clover vs. Square at Restaurant Volume

This is where the comparison gets real, because processing — not software — is the biggest line item for almost every restaurant.

**Square's published rates (squareup.com, June 2026):**

* Card-present: **2.6% + 15¢** (Free), **2.5% + 15¢** (Plus), **2.4% + 15¢** (Premium)
* Online: **3.3% + 30¢** (Free), **2.9% + 30¢** (Plus/Premium)
* Keyed/card-on-file: **3.5% + 15¢**

Worth knowing: the Free plan's online rate rose from 2.9% + 30¢ to 3.3% + 30¢ effective January 13, 2026. If a meaningful share of your sales comes through online ordering and you're on Square Free, that change quietly added 0.4 points to those orders — one more reason to re-run your plan math annually.

**Clover's rates, as reported by NerdWallet and Tech.co (June 2026):**

* Card-present on restaurant plans: **2.3% + 10¢**
* Keyed/card-not-present: **3.5% + 10¢**

A caveat that cuts both ways: because Clover is also sold through banks and resellers, the rate on your actual quote can differ from list — sometimes better, sometimes worse.

### The Worked Example

Take a restaurant doing **$40,000 a month in card-present volume at a $30 average ticket** — about 1,333 transactions.

| Setup | Processing | Software | Total/mo |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Square Free (2.6% + 15¢) | $1,240 | $0 | ~$1,240 |
| Square Plus (2.5% + 15¢) | $1,200 | $49 | ~$1,249 |
| Square Premium (2.4% + 15¢) | $1,160 | $149 | ~$1,309 |
| Clover restaurant plan (2.3% + 10¢, as reported) | $1,053 | $89.95 | ~$1,143 |

At this volume, Clover's lower rate saves roughly **$100 a month, about $1,200 a year**, even after its higher software fee.

But flip the volume and the answer flips. At a $30 ticket, Clover's rate advantage over Square Free is worth about 0.47¢ per dollar processed, so the break-even sits around **$19,000–$20,000 a month in card-present volume**. Below that, Square Free is usually cheaper in total. Above it, Clover pulls ahead and keeps pulling.

Three caveats before you treat that as gospel: this ignores online-order volume (different rates on both systems), it ignores hardware, and Clover's actual rate depends on your seller. The point isn't the exact crossover — it's that **the right answer is a function of your volume**, which is why generic "which is cheaper" listicles can't answer it for you. Total cost of ownership is the ROI math that matters.

**Want the same kind of math run on your whole digital ordering operation — not just processing?** [Get a Demo](/get-demo/) and we'll show you what operators on your POS actually make back.

## Hardware Costs

**Square** sells direct, with financing on bigger items:

* Magstripe reader — first one free
* Square Reader (contactless/chip) — $59
* Square Stand — $149 (or $14/mo × 12)
* Square Terminal — $299 (or $27/mo × 12)
* Square Handheld — $399 (or $37/mo × 12)
* Square Register — $899 (or $44/mo × 24)

**Clover** hardware, as reported (June 2026):

* Clover Go — $199
* Clover Flex (handheld) — from around $649 (Square's comparison page lists $649; NerdWallet and Merchant Maverick list $749 — confirm with your seller)
* Clover Mini — $849
* Station Solo — $1,799
* Station Duo — $1,899

Clover hardware can be bought upfront or rolled into 36-month payment plans. Some bank channels have historically offered hardware leases — read those terms carefully, since leasing hardware over several years usually costs more than buying it.

**Restaurant takeaway:** Square owns the low end — nothing in Clover's lineup competes with a free magstripe reader or a $59 contactless reader for a stall, popup, or truck. Clover's hardware is purpose-built, countertop-grade kit, and its flagship stations are priced like it. For a full station build-out, expect Clover to cost more upfront and Square to cost more per swipe.

## Restaurant Features Head-to-Head

### Kitchen Display Systems

Square's KDS is an app you license per device: **$30/device/mo on Plus, $20/device/mo on Premium**, and not available on the Free plan. Per Square's restaurant page, it supports ticket customization, automatic 86ing of sold-out items, and prep-time insights. Clover includes KDS capability in its higher restaurant bundles, per Tech.co — confirm exactly which tier includes it when you get a quote, because tier packaging is the kind of detail that varies by seller.

If your kitchen runs on tickets and timing — and whose doesn't — price the KDS into your comparison, not as an afterthought. Two KDS screens on Square Plus is $60/mo on top of the $49 plan; that changes the software-cost gap with Clover considerably.

### Online Ordering

Clover includes online ordering with its restaurant plans at no added software cost, per NerdWallet. Square offers Square Online, which has a free tier and charges the online processing rate (3.3% + 30¢ on Free since January 2026, 2.9% + 30¢ on Plus/Premium).

Here's the operator's framing: the built-in ordering page is table stakes either way. What actually moves profitability is whether your 1st-party channel — your website, your Google listing, your repeat-customer engine — wins orders that would otherwise go to 3rd-party marketplaces at full commission. That's a marketing and integration problem more than a POS feature problem, and it's solvable on both systems (it's the problem [Chowly exists to solve](/chowly-platform/)).

### Table Management, Coursing, and Checks

Square's restaurant feature set (Plus and up, per its restaurant page) covers coursing, tableside ordering, and split checks by item, seat, or equal share, plus menu import from a PDF or an existing delivery-platform menu — genuinely useful when you're migrating. Clover's full-service plans are built around table service, and its top FSR bundle ships with a Station Duo plus a Flex handheld for tableside work, per Tech.co. At the Advanced tiers, both systems are credible for a full-service room; the difference shows up in how you pay for it, not whether it exists.

### Handhelds

Square Handheld runs $399 (or $37/mo × 12). Clover Flex starts from around $649 as reported. Both take orders and payments tableside. If handhelds for every server are central to your service model, the per-unit gap multiplies fast — four handhelds is roughly a $1,000+ difference in upfront hardware.

## How They're Sold: The Difference That Matters Most

This is the part the generic comparisons bury, and for restaurants it's arguably the most consequential difference between the two companies. It's not a feature — it's a buying process.

**Square sells one way:** direct, self-serve, published pricing, no long-term contract. You can sign up tonight, try Plus free for 30 days, and quit next month. What you see on the pricing page is what you pay. The trade-off for that simplicity is that the published rate is the rate — there's little negotiating until you're big enough for custom pricing.

**Clover, a Fiserv company, sells three ways:** direct on clover.com (one-time hardware purchase or 36-month payment plans), through bank partners such as Wells Fargo and PNC, and through independent resellers and ISOs. Per Merchant Maverick (November 2025), pricing, contract length, and support quality all vary by seller, and reseller agreements commonly run 36 to 48 months with early-termination fees.

Stated neutrally, because it genuinely cuts both ways: the multi-channel model means a strong local reseller can deliver negotiated rates, in-person installs, and same-day support that no self-serve vendor matches. It also means two restaurants on identical Clover hardware can be paying very different rates on very different terms.

The practical buying advice, whichever direction you lean:

* **Buying Clover:** get the contract length, early-termination fee, processing rate, and monthly software fee in writing before you sign. Compare your reseller or bank quote against clover.com list pricing. A great quote is great — confirm it survives the paperwork.
* **Buying Square:** know which plan you're on and what its online rate is — especially after the January 2026 Free-plan change — and re-check the plan math as your volume grows. At some point Premium's lower rates beat Plus.

## Which Should Your Restaurant Pick?

No single winner — the honest answer depends on your format and your volume.

### Counter-Service and QSR

Lower tickets, higher transaction counts, less need for coursing and table maps. Square's $0 entry and cheap hardware make it the default starting point, and the per-transaction fee gap (15¢ vs 10¢) only starts to sting at serious volume. A high-volume QSR doing well past the ~$20K/month crossover should price out Clover's QSR plans — the rate savings are real money at scale.

### Full-Service Restaurants

Coursing, table management, handhelds, KDS — both deliver, but the costs stack differently. On Square, the FSR feature set means Plus or Premium plus per-device KDS fees; on Clover, it means the higher FSR tiers where more is bundled. Higher average tickets also shrink the relative weight of the per-transaction fee and amplify the percentage rate, which works in Clover's favor as volume climbs. Run the worked-example math above with your own numbers; for many established FSRs it tilts Clover, while FSRs that value month-to-month flexibility stay with Square.

### Food Trucks

The r/foodtrucks crowd debates this constantly, and the economics say: start with Square. A free plan plus a $59 reader (or a $299 Terminal for receipts and reliability) is the cheapest credible setup in the industry, with no contract if the concept doesn't survive the season. A proven truck with strong steady volume can revisit Clover Go ($199) and the lower rates once there's a year of sales data to justify the software fee.

### Multi-Location Operators

Square's per-location pricing ($49 or $149 per location) is transparent and scales predictably, and centralized menu and reporting tools are solid. Clover multi-location deals typically run through a reseller or bank relationship, where per-location terms are negotiated — which can land cheaper than list, with more contract to manage. At 3+ locations, get both quotes in writing and compare total cost over 36 months, since that's the term you're likely signing on one side anyway.

**Choose Square if:** you want $0 or low software cost to start, month-to-month flexibility, the cheapest hardware entry point, published pricing with no negotiation, or you're a truck, popup, or first location proving the concept.

**Choose Clover if:** your card-present volume is comfortably past the crossover (~$19K–$20K/month at a $30 ticket), you want online ordering and restaurant features bundled into the base restaurant plans, you value a local reseller or bank relationship for install and support, and you're comfortable committing to a multi-year term in exchange for lower rates.

## Whichever You Pick, Chowly Runs on Top of It

Here's the part where we stop being neutral about POS and start being direct about what we do: Chowly is POS-native with both systems. Orders from your branded website, your mobile app, your Google listing, and 3rd-party marketplaces flow straight into [Square](/pos/chowly-for-square/) or [Clover](/pos/chowly-for-clover/) and print in the kitchen like any other ticket — no tablet farm, no manual re-keying.

On top of that integration, the Chowly Platform runs the demand side: [branded online ordering](/solutions/branded-online-ordering/), managed [Google Ads](/solutions/paid-ads/) tracked to confirmed POS orders (so ROI is measured in actual revenue, not clicks), email marketing, loyalty, and [dynamic pricing](/solutions/dynamic-pricing/). Liv's Juice & Acai Bar, a two-location Square operator in Massachusetts, used it to grow 1st-party digital sales +17% year over year and save **$121K annually in third-party commissions** — and as co-owner Neil Paris put it, "Now that orders print directly from our Square POS, I can't imagine going back." [Read the Liv's Juice case study](/resources/case-studies/livs-juice-and-acai-bar-x-chowly-platform/).

And if your shortlist is really "Toast vs Square vs Clover," same answer applies — Chowly is POS-native with [Toast](/pos/chowly-for-toast/) too, along with 50+ other systems. Pick the POS that fits how you operate; the growth layer works either way.

## FAQ

### Is Clover better or Square?

Neither is better across the board. Square is lower-cost to start, with a free entry plan, transparent self-serve pricing, and hardware from $59. Clover charges more for software but offers lower card-present rates on its restaurant plans (2.3% + 10¢ as reported, vs Square's 2.6% + 15¢ on its free tier) and includes online ordering. The right answer depends on your format, card volume, and how you prefer to buy.

### What's cheaper, Clover or Square?

It depends on volume. At a $30 average ticket, a restaurant processing under roughly $19,000–$20,000 a month in card-present sales usually pays less in total on Square's free plan. Above that, Clover's lower per-transaction rate typically outruns its higher software fee. Run the math on your own numbers, and remember Clover pricing can vary by where you buy it.

### What POS system is better, Clover or Square?

For restaurants specifically: counter-service spots and food trucks tend to favor Square for its free plan and cheap hardware, while higher-volume and full-service restaurants tend to favor Clover for its lower card-present rates and bundled online ordering. Both are credible restaurant POS systems, and both work with Chowly.

### Are Clover's processing fees lower than Square's?

On card-present transactions, yes, as of June 2026. Clover's restaurant plans run 2.3% + 10¢ per reported pricing, while Square charges 2.6% + 15¢ on its free plan, 2.5% + 15¢ on Plus, and 2.4% + 15¢ on Premium. But Clover's software fees are higher, so compare total monthly cost, not just the rate.

### Does Square or Clover require a contract?

Square has no long-term contract — you pay month to month and can cancel anytime. Clover depends on where you buy: direct from clover.com means a one-time hardware purchase or a 36-month payment plan, while bank and reseller channels commonly involve 36–48 month agreements with early-termination fees. Always confirm contract length and exit terms in writing.

### Which is better for a food truck, Square or Clover?

Most food trucks start with Square because the free plan plus a $59 reader or $299 terminal is the cheapest credible setup in the industry. A high-volume truck doing steady card-present sales may save money on Clover's lower rates with a $199 Clover Go, but the software fee has to earn its keep first.

### Can I use Chowly with Square or Clover?

Yes — both. Chowly is POS-native with Square and Clover, meaning online orders from your website, app, and 3rd-party marketplaces flow straight into the POS and print in the kitchen like any other ticket. Whichever system you pick, the Chowly Platform runs on top of it.

<webpage_content>
Credit Card Processing

# Clover vs Square: Which should you choose?

![Ben Dwyer](https://www.gravatar.com/avatar/45d01cf4f9ca0765088e9c72346473c9?s=96) By [Ben Dwyer](/blog/author/bdwyercardfellow-com)

See the **best rates** from multiple  
processors instantly!

 [Sign up free & see!](/sign-up)

* [Clover POS vs. Square POS](#POS)
* [Clover Mini vs. Square Stand](#ministand)
* [Clover Station vs. Square Register](#stationregister)
