**Clover** (sold by Fiserv through resellers) offers the broadest hardware ecosystem (Station, Mini, Flex, Mobile, Kiosk) but suffers from opaque pricing, reseller lock-in, 3-year contracts, and Marketplace app costs that accumulate over time. Best for retail-restaurant hybrids like cafes with retail sales, breweries, and food markets.

**Katalyst OS** (built by restaurateurs) is presented as the restaurant-native alternative. It offers interchange-plus transparent processing, bundled features (catering, branded mobile app, kiosk, reservations, open API), no processor lock-in, and annual or month-to-month contracts. Best for multi-location operations (3+), catering-heavy concepts, and restaurants outgrowing Square or Clover.

**Pricing comparison** for a typical $1.5M annual volume single-location restaurant: Square ~$900–1,200/month, Clover ~$700–1,400/month (reseller-variable), Katalyst ~$700–1,000/month. Average Katalyst client saves $55K+/year.

The page also promotes a free rate analysis service where operators can submit merchant statements to compare costs.

* **ISO margins vary dramatically: Toast offers 20–35% software rev share, Clover 15–30%, Lightspeed 25–40%, while Square’s partner program is the least flexible.**

For an ISO or POS reseller, choosing the right platform partner is the single most important business decision. Sign with the wrong platform and you will fight high churn, low margins, and constant merchant complaints. Pick the right one and your portfolio compounds like clockwork. This guide compares the four dominant POS platforms — Toast, Clover, Square, and Lightspeed — from an ISO’s perspective, not a merchant’s.

## 1. Toast: The Restaurant Specialist

**Best for:** ISOs focused exclusively on full-service and quick-service restaurants

Toast is the 800-pound gorilla in restaurant POS, with ~35% market share among full-service restaurants and over 100,000 locations on its platform. For ISOs, it offers the most restaurant-specific functionality and highest enterprise-level credibility.

**Pros for ISOs:**

* Deep restaurant features: kitchen display, tableside ordering, tip pooling, delivery integration
* Strong brand recognition — merchants often come to ISOs asking for Toast
* 20–35% software subscription rev share (higher for proprietary processing bundle)
* Enterprise-grade reporting and analytics

**Cons for ISOs:**

* Restaurant-only — cannot sell to retail, salon, or other verticals
* Hardware costs are high ($1,500–$3,000 per station)
* Exclusive processing requirements limit ISO’s ability to offer alternative pricing
* Training and support burden on ISO — Toast provides limited white-glove onboarding

## 2. Clover: The SMB Generalist

**Best for:** ISOs serving general retail, quick-service restaurants, and professional services

Owned by Fiserv (formerly First Data), Clover is the most widely distributed POS platform in the U.S. with over 2 million devices deployed. Its flexibility across verticals and broad ISO/reseller network make it the default choice for many ISOs.

**Pros for ISOs:**

* Works across retail, restaurant, service, and professional verticals
* Multiple hardware tiers (Clover Go, Flex, Mini, Station) from $299–$1,399
* 15–30% rev share on software and processing; plus residual income on processing volume
* Fiserv processing backbone — stable, reliable, and compliant

**Cons for ISOs:**

* Limited customization — merchants cannot brand the dashboard as their own
* App market fragmentation — third-party apps add complexity and support overhead
* Competition from Fiserv’s direct sales force and large ISOs
* Relatively low switching costs for merchants — churn risk higher than vertical-specific platforms

**ISO Pro Tip:** Clover is the best entry point for new ISOs because of its lowest barrier to entry and broadest merchant appeal. Upgrade to vertical-specific platforms as your portfolio matures.

## 3. Square: The Ecosystem Player

**Best for:** ISOs targeting micro-businesses and pop-up merchants

Square (Block, Inc.) has 6+ million active sellers but operates more as a sales channel than a traditional POS partner. Its ISO partner program is the least developed of the four platforms.

**Pros for ISOs:**

* Massive brand awareness — merchants know Square; easy introductory conversation
* Lowest hardware cost ($0 reader, $49 Stand, $169 Terminal)
* Rich ecosystem: Square Online, Square Payroll, Square Banking, Square Capital
* Flat-rate pricing (2.6% + $0.10) is simple to understand and sell

**Cons for ISOs:**

* Lowest ISO margins — no residual income on processing; referral fee only
* Merchants can sign up directly — ISO adds zero friction in the acquisition funnel
* No vertical-specific features — Square for Restaurants lags Toast significantly
* Limited hardware options for high-volume merchants

## 4. Lightspeed: The Specialty Retail Powerhouse

**Best for:** ISOs focused on specialty retail (bikes, sporting goods, apparel, pet, outdoor)

Lightspeed dominates the specialty retail segment with inventory management features that general-purpose POS systems cannot match. Its ISO partner program offers the highest residual splits of any major platform.

**Pros for ISOs:**

* 25–40% software rev share — highest of the four platforms
* Best-in-class inventory management (multi-location, serial tracking, vendor management)
* eCommerce integration (Lightspeed Online) is the strongest native offering
* Less ISO competition — fewer resellers in the specialty retail space

**Cons for ISOs:**

* Higher subscription cost ($69–$169/location/month) — may deter micro-merchants
* Narrow vertical focus — not suitable for restaurants, salons, or general retail
* Smaller brand recognition vs. Toast, Clover, or Square
* Implementation complexity — requires more training and onboarding effort

| Merchant Retention | High | Medium | Low | High |
| Processing Flexibility | Captive | Semi-flexible | Captive | Flexible |
| Overall ISO Score | 4.2/5 | 4.5/5 | 3.0/5 | 4.0/5 |

## 6. Which Platform Should You Choose?

There is no single right answer. The best platform depends on your portfolio strategy:

* **Starting out:** Partner with Clover for broad merchant appeal and low entry barrier
* **Restaurant specialist:** Toast — unparalleled features and brand trust
* **Specialty retail focus:** Lightspeed — best margins and deepest features
* **Micro-merchant strategy:** Square — easy to acquire, but low margins
* **Multi-platform ISO:** Offer 2–3 platforms based on merchant vertical to maximize portfolio diversity

If you are considering a white-label alternative that gives you full brand control and better margins than any of these platforms, explore **OrderPin’s ISO program**.

## Bottom Line

The platform wars in POS are not about which platform is “best” — they are about which platform is best for your ISO business model. Evaluate based on your target vertical, your support capacity, and your margin requirements. The wrong platform will cost you merchants; the right one will compound your revenue.

# Toast POS: Everything You Need To Know 2025

Toast POS is a comprehensive technological solution for the restaurant industry that integrates with Deliverect Restaurants. In this essential guide, Toast POS 101, we explore its key features and provide strategic recommendations for fully leveraging its potential.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHdpZHRoPSIxMjAiIGhlaWdodD0iMTIwIj48L3N2Zz4=)![](data:image/png;base64,)

* [4 TIPS TO GET THE MOST OUT OF TOAST](#section-4-tips-to-get-the-most-out-of-toast)

Toast is an all-in-one platform crafted for the dining sector. It covers everything from a point-of-sale system (POS) to advanced technology, facilitating digital orders, deliveries, and marketing strategies for businesses of different sizes, from independent cafés to bars, food trucks, and restaurant chains.

You’re adopting Toast, which will not just enhance your restaurant operations with an Android-based POS system. You're also driving efficiency and innovation in the sector, positioning your business for growth and success. Let’s delve into the benefits your business can reap from using this platform.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHdpZHRoPSIyMTUwIiBoZWlnaHQ9IjgwNiI+PC9zdmc+)![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

## **INTRODUCING TOAST**

### **What is TOAST?**

Toast POS system is a complete cloud-based software and hardware solution for restaurants. It encompasses point-of-sale systems and payments, digital operations, and team management software. It also offers advanced staff management tools and financing options through Toast Capital to foster business growth.

With its headquarters in Boston, United States, and founded in 2012, Toast has seen significant expansion, serving over 106,000 restaurants in markets across the U.S., Canada, Ireland, and the United Kingdom.

Its outstanding performance is reflected in its inclusion in the [Forbes Cloud 100 list](https://pos.toasttab.com/news/toast-named-to-the-2021-forbes-cloud-100) for 2021 and recognition as one of the [top POS systems by the G2 platform](https://www.g2.com/categories/restaurant-pos#grid), known for its software reviews and comparisons.

## **TOAST PRICING**

The pricing of [Toast POS](/en-us/integrations/toast) is designed with flexibility in mind to accommodate a broad range of establishments.

The cost determination for restaurants involves:

* **Monthly Subscription Costs:** A monthly fee covering hardware and software in monthly payment options.
* **Payment Processing Charges:** A percentage fee per transaction and an additional payment processing fee apply.
* **Extra Costs and Add-ons:** Restaurants can customize and add additional software and hardware solutions, which are payable monthly and add to the total monthly cost.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHdpZHRoPSIyMTUwIiBoZWlnaHQ9IjgwNiI+PC9zdmc+)![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

## **PLAN OPTIONS**

Toast offers four plan options. The Starter Kit can be purchased directly from the website, while the other three require a demo request or a quote via the site, as they are customizable. The Toast pricing section provides a detailed feature comparison of each plan.

**Toast’s Plans:**

1. Starter Kit
2. Point of Sale
3. Build Your Own
4. Restaurant Special Offer

All plans come with regular updates, a cloud-based POS system, and 24/7 customer support via phone, email, or chat. Moreover, all plans offer payment processing with real-time fraud monitoring and training services.

### **TOAST Starter Kit**

The Toast Starter Kit brings up to two terminals and is perfect for individual locations. It’s available in Pay-as-you-Go and Standard purchase options.

The Starter Kit includes:

* Toast Flex POS Terminal
* Toast Tap Payment Device
* Router
* POS Software
* Free Installation support

### **TOAST STARTER KIT - PAY-AS-YOU-GO**

This option allows restaurants to start [without upfront costs](https://pos.toasttab.com/shop/starter-kits/countertop-starter-kit); it includes the necessary hardware and software. Three options are available for purchasing the kit, which has a fee based on transaction rates.

**Option 1: Pay-as-you-Go**

* Upfront: $0.00
* Monthly fee: $0.00
* Transaction fee: 3.09% + 15¢

**Option 2: Pay-as-you-Go Core**

* Upfront: $0.00
* Monthly fee: $0.00
* Transaction fee: 3.39% + 15¢
* It includes the Starter Kit benefits, plus online ordering and Integration Bundle with DoorDash, Grubhub, or Uber Eats.

**Option 3: Pay-as-you-Go Growth**

* Upfront: $0.00
* Monthly fee: $0.00 Transaction fee: 3.69% + 15¢ It includes everything from Core, plus features like Gift Cards, Loyalty, Email Marketing, Websites, and Catering and events.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHdpZHRoPSIxNzkyIiBoZWlnaHQ9IjY3MiI+PC9zdmc+)![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

### **TOAST STARTER KIT - STANDARD**

Purchasing this kit involves an upfront payment for hardware and monthly payments for software, including a transaction fee and a base monthly cost, which can increase with additional features.

* Upfront: $1,024.20
* Monthly fee: $69
* Transaction fee: 2.49% + 15¢
* This package allows you to install hardware and feature add-ons beyond what comes with the Starter Kit.
* Rates under this plan vary depending on the type of transaction and the manner of payment.

> **Note:** Prices are based on U.S. rates. Select the country on the page to view plans in other countries; pricing and availability may vary.

## **REGISTERING AND SETUP**

Obtaining Toast’s products is straightforward and customizable. You can incorporate add-on features or specific integrations tailored to your business needs.

As mentioned in the plans section, you can sign up directly on the web for the Starter Kit. However, to access the other three plans, you should follow these steps to request a demo or quote:

1. Visit the [Toast website](https://pos.toasttab.com/request-demo-intl).
2. Fill out the registration form.
3. A Toast representative will contact you within 24 hours to provide a demo, answer your questions, and help you select the most suitable plan.
4. Once a plan is purchased, Toast will help you set up and train you and your staff.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHdpZHRoPSIxNzkyIiBoZWlnaHQ9IjY3MiI+PC9zdmc+)![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

## **FEATURES / SOLUTIONS**

Toast offers an extensive catalog of products ranging from software and hardware to financing options. We list the primary services in each of their categories below:

**Software:**

To enhance operations, customer interactions, cost management, and ultimately, profit margins and customer contentment, Toast offers a suite of Android-based software solutions, including:

* Point-of-sale System (POS)
* Inventory
* Reporting and Analytics
* Toast Delivery Services
* Payroll & Team Management
* Toast Mobile Order & Pay

**Hardware:**

Toast’s meticulously designed hardware offers versatility and efficiency, from mobile devices to robust workstations, suitable for various settings from the checkout to the kitchen.

* Kiosk
* Toast Flex
* Toast Flex for Kitchen

### **Toast Payments Solutions:**

### **Toast Services:**

Beyond hardware and software, Toast provides extensive support and implementation services, addressing technical concerns and offering insights into product utilization. Additionally, Toast offers accessible capital lending services for financial flexibility.

## **STANDOUT ADVANTAGES**

Beyond its software and hardware benefits, Toast offers notable solutions that include:

### **Local Driver Network Delivery**

Toast Delivery Services allows restaurants to conduct home deliveries utilizing an on-demand network of local drivers, removing the worry about driver availability. It facilitates real-time tracking and allows scheduling orders in advance, ensuring a smooth experience for restaurants and customers. This feature is accessible for online orders and Toast Takeout users.

### **Access to Loans via Toast**

Restaurants can access loans through Toast Capital for various needs, such as renovations, inventory acquisition, or equipment purchases. With payment terms ranging from 90 to 360 days, restaurants can check their loan eligibility online. Once the process is complete and the application is approved, they can receive the funds the next business day. Loan repayments are a percentage of the restaurant’s daily card sales.

### **Real-Time, Accessible Reporting with Toast**

Offering real-time visibility on any device, Toast’s mobile-friendly interface ensures convenience regardless of location. Features include receiving a daily email summary with crucial performance metrics each night, allowing for total and easy access to restaurant data.

### **Toast Now App**

Offering swift access to real-time analytics, the Toast Now mobile app is downloadable from [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.toasttab.toastoperator&hl=en_US) and the [Apple Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/toast-now/id6444586410) using Toast Web login details. It allows for detailed sales and labor costs reports by the hour and includes a messaging dashboard for efficient staff communication.

## **POS INTEGRATIONS**

[Toast enables seamless integration](/en-us/integrations/toast) with various leading applications and services, enhancing the restaurant’s operational capabilities from delivery platforms to loyalty and accounting solutions. These integrations can be acquired as add-on features to existing plans.

The partnership between Toast and Deliverect Restaurants centralizes orders from multiple delivery platforms into Toast’s POS system. This facilitates a unified view of all transactions, streamlined menu and inventory management, and the generation of insightful analytics reports that pinpoint strengths and improvement opportunities. This integration requires active subscriptions to both Toast and Deliverect Restaurants.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHdpZHRoPSIyODY4IiBoZWlnaHQ9Ijk0NiI+PC9zdmc+)![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

## **4 TIPS TO GET THE MOST OUT OF TOAST**

### **Tip 1: Enhance Hospitality with Reservation Management**

Enhance your customers’ dining experience with Toast Tables, a powerful solution seamlessly integrated with Toast POS for efficient reservation and waitlist management. Guests can easily book their tables through Google and Maps, while communication is enhanced through personalized SMS notifications. Elevate the experience for your VIP customers by offering tailored attention, ensuring their visit is nothing short of extraordinary.

### **Tip 2: Engage Customers with Effective Email Campaigns**

You can use thoughtful email marketing from Toast to ensure that people remember your restaurant. Deliver automated, personalized emails featuring enticing promotions and maintain a regular rhythm without overwhelming your subscribers. Based on Toast’s research, monthly updates tend to be well-received by most customers. Explore the effectiveness of your campaigns through A/B testing, audience segmentation, and comprehensive analytics tracking open rates, click-through rates, and conversion rates.

### **Tip 3: Increase Revenue and Loyalty with Gift Cards**

Strengthen customer loyalty and diversify your income with Toast’s gift cards. This feature, available as an add-on if not included in your current plan, simplifies the sale, tracking, and management of physical and electronic cards from the POS and online. Attract new customers and reward regulars.

### **Tip 4: Grow with Toast’s Comprehensive Resources**

Make the most of all Toast resources, from insightful blogs and eBooks to free templates and business-specific webinars. These tools are crucial for training your team, optimizing your Toast usage, and gaining insights into the restaurant industry.

Implementing Toast will transform your restaurant, opening the doors to a comprehensive ecosystem to refine your business management. Its user-friendly interface and broad catalog of tools will help enhance operational efficiency. Toast’s ability to easily integrate with third-party apps, fully customizable loyalty and marketing programs, and the flexibility to adapt and expand your services as needed make It an essential ally.

> The partnership between [Toast and Deliverect Restaurants](/en-us/integrations/toast) streamlines various tasks, particularly in delivery management, by consolidating orders from diverse platforms into one system via the POS. This integration provides a reliable and satisfying experience by reducing errors and consistently meeting their service and quality standards.

Explore the vast possibilities with Toast and take a step toward digital transformation for your restaurant.

[Back to top](#top)

[Back to top](#top)

[Back to top](#top)

[Back to top](#top)

* **11" L x 15" W x 3.5" H**
* **27.9 cm L x 38.1 cm W x 8.9 cm H**

[Back to top](#top)

The dimensions of the Zebra DS2208 scanner (without the cradle) are

* **3.9" L x 2.6" W x 6.5" H**
* **9.9 cm L x 6.6 cm W x 16.5 cm H**

The dimensions of the Zebra DS2278 wireless scanner (without the cradle) are

* **3.5" L x 2.6" W x 6.9" H**
* **9 cm L x 6.6 cm W x 17.5 cm H**

The dimensions of the Zebra DS9308 scanner are

* **3.3" L x 3.4" W x 5.7" H**
* **8.3 cm L x 8.6 cm W x 14.5 cm H**

[Back to top](#top)

### Toast Cash Drawer

The dimensions of a Toast cash drawer are:

* **41 cm L x 41.5 cm W x 11.3 cm H**
* We recommend a **12" (31.3 cm)** clearance in front of the drawer to fully open it.

Toast, best known for its restaurant software at this point, just announced a suite of point-of-sale (POS) hardware tools designed by the company itself. Simply dubbed Toast Hardware, the suite consists of four different devices, according to the company’s press announcement. This is the first way in which the company is using money from its [recent $400 million fundraise](https://thespoon.tech/toast-announces-400m-in-fresh-funds-now-has-a-4-9b-valuation/) that bumped the company’s valuation up to $4.9 billion.

The main device of the four is the Toast Flex terminal, a POS terminal with a 14-inch screen that works across different contexts in the restaurant, including the front of house and the kitchen. It can integrate with another new piece of hardware, Toast Tap, which is an external payment processing device that supports NFC (contactless payments), EMV (chip), MSR (swipe) forms of payment. Toast Printer and Toast Hub, meanwhile, are aimed at eliminating cable clutter from hardware and allow the restaurant to set the entire hardware configuration up in a few minutes.

This actually isn’t Toast’s first foray into the hardware space. The company [released its handheld payment device](https://pos.toasttab.com/news/toastgo-toastkds), ToastGo, in 2018.

Nor are these likely to be the last pieces of hardware the company designs and releases to the restaurant industry. From the point of view of a restaurant chain, having interoperable hardware and software pieces that come from the same vendor solves a major issue in the restaurant biz right now, which is that there’s plenty of technology from plenty different vendors, but most devices aren’t great at talking to one another. Terrible, in fact.

Buying a hardware suite from one company and using the accompanying software means there’s a greater chance a restaurant’s different devices and software can communicate smoothly and that the GM won’t have to play the role of de facto IT person during a busy dinner rush. (Of course, the flip side of that is that restaurants would lock themselves in with a single vendor.)

From Toast’s point of view, offering more hardware in addition to its software and [extensive partner marketplace](https://pos.toasttab.com/solutions/partner-ecosystem) keeps Toast customers firmly entrenched in the company’s own world. It also lets Toast more adequately compete with others in the crowded POS space, Square, Revel, and Clover among them.

# Toast Pricing: How Much Does This POS System Cost? [2026]

I’ll give you a detailed background of what you can expect to pay with the Toast platform.

11 min readJune 4, 2026

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/69b9330c8b70142e4e5f7d3d/69b9330c8b70142e4e5f891e_Untitled-hero-770x513%20(1).jpg)

Key takeaways

* Toast pricing varies by plan, but all plans include both upfront hardware expenses and ongoing payment processing fees.
* All Toast plans offer 24/7 support, flexible payment options, offline mode and a simple and fast setup.
* Toast has some drawbacks like additional hardware costs, only offers basic online ordering as an add-on and can be harder to set up than other platforms.
* There are several tools to consider other than Toast, like Clover, Owner and Square.

‍

[Toast](https://pos.toasttab.com/pricing) is a popular POS system that handles orders, processes payments, manages online ordering and even automates marketing.

For busy restaurant owners, a system like Toast can be a game-changer. It simplifies day-to-day operations, improves team coordination, and gives guests a smoother experience at the counter, table, or online.

What sets Toast apart? It’s especially strong when it comes to streamlining your back office. From payroll to inventory to real-time sales data, Toast helps you stay on top of the business side so you can focus on your food and your guests.

That said, a POS system is a big investment, so it’s worth making sure Toast fits your budget and aligns with your financial goals. You may even find that a different platform is a better fit based on your restaurant’s size, setup, or service model.

In this guide, I’ll break down exactly what Toast costs, what you get with each plan, the pros and cons to consider, and how it stacks up against top alternatives.

## **Toast pricing breakdown**

It's super important for restaurant owners to know the Toast POS fees and pricing structure because it helps you plan and budget right from the start.

Knowing the costs upfront lets you see if Toast works for your restaurant and fits your financial goals as you grow. Let me break down Toast’s pricing plans below:

![Toast pricing structure](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/666eec3edcc552b5eecc7fcd/68265b77b348c9b4e051f711_toast-pricing-structure-mobile.png)

And here are the features that all three plans include:

* One flat rate
* Real-time fraud monitoring
* 24/7/365 customer support
* Installation and network configuration
* Automatic feature and software upgrades
* Table and order management
* Digital menus, offline mode and mobile payments
* Integrated PCI-compliant payments and surcharging
* Timekeeping, announcements and newsfeed, and basic scheduling

**Note:** There are upfront costs you have to pay Toast when you implement any of these plans. You also have to pay for the hardware separately. This will vary depending on which package you choose and installation needs.

### **Starter Kit**

**Cost:** Free—*additional fees will apply for hardware and onboarding*

As the name suggests, the Starter Plan is made for new restaurants that just need a simple, affordable POS system to get started. If you’re running a food truck, pop-up, or a small cafe with one location, this plan could be exactly what you need.

It’s also a great option if you’re new to Toast and want to test the waters to see if it’s a good long-term fit for your business.

With this Starter Kit, you’ll get restaurant-grade hardware, and you can choose between a terminal or handheld kit. The hardware connects to one location and supports up to two terminals—perfect for a smaller setup.

Some of the essentials I really like in this plan include order management, payment processing and basic reporting tools to keep things running smoothly.

Although the website states the plan itself is free, it does require upfront hardware and onboarding costs which I'll mention later.

You can also customize this plan with optional add-ons at an additional charge like:

* Toast Mobile Order & Pay
* Partner Connect
* Third-party delivery integrations
* Digital Storefront Suite
* Payroll Suite
* Scheduling & Team Communication
* Supplier & Accounting Suite

It’s simple, flexible and designed to grow with your needs.

**Pro tip:** This plan offers a Pay-as-You-Go plan with an all-in-one platform rate that lowers your upfront hardware and installation costs.

### **Point of Sale**

**Cost:** $69 per month

The Point of Sale plan costs $69 per month for the software, and you can choose your hardware setup. Unlike the Starter Kit, this plan gives you more flexibility—perfect if you’re looking to customize your setup or need to manage more than one restaurant location.

It includes everything in the Starter Kit but with even more add-on options (for an extra cost), like:

* Toast Mobile Order & Pay
* Retail POS Suite
* Toast Scheduling Pro and Tips Manager
* Supplier and Accounting Suite (with handy tools like food cost analytics and invoice automation)

One thing I really like? There’s a demo available, so you can try it out before committing.

This plan is ideal if your restaurant is more established and you’re ready for more advanced features or need a setup that can grow with your business. Plus, it’s a great choice if you’re running multiple locations and want a POS system that keeps everything connected.

### **Build Your Own**

**Cost:** Depends on customization preferences

If you already have a clear vision of what you need in a POS system and want full control to customize your plan, the Build Your Own plan might be perfect for you. It comes with the entire suite of Toast features, letting you pick and choose exactly what works best for your restaurant.

**Note:** There are upfront costs you have to pay Toast when you implement any of these plans. You also have to pay for the hardware separately. This will vary depending on which package you choose andyour installation needs. I’ll cover this more below, as well as what a few of the integrations cost.

## **What you’ll pay upfront with Toast: Hardware and setup fees**

Let’s talk about what it actually costs to get started with Toast. Even though their pricing plans are billed monthly, there are still some pretty hefty one-time fees to get up and running.

In a recent demo call with Toast, I got a full breakdown of the upfront expenses, including onboarding and hardware. So let’s break that down first, then we’ll look at the ongoing charges for software and integrations.

### **Onboarding**

Toast charges $849 just to get set up with 1-2 tablets. Digital ordering will run another $100. And converting gift cards to the new system will also cost you $100.

**Total onboarding fees:** $1,049

### **Hardware**

Now let’s talk hardware. Here’s what you’ll need to budget for if you’re outfitting your setup with Toast equipment:

* 14" Toast flex with Counter Stand, Toast Tap, Toast Printer and Cash Drawer: **$1,049**
* 14" Toast Flex for Kitchen and Wall Mount: **$749**
* Meraki Z4 Router: **$449**
* 8 Port Ethernet Switch: **$59**
* Toast Kitchen Printer: **$339**

**Total hardware cost:** $2,645

‍

So, just to get started with Toast, you can expect to pay **$3,694.**

## **Toast recurring costs: Software and integrations**

Once you’ve covered the upfront costs, you’ll still have some monthly charges to factor in. **Software recurring costs are $90 monthly.** And, if you want to take advantage of their integration options, here’s a breakdown of those costs:

* Toast Marketing Essentials (this includes Gift Card, Loyalty Program, and their base email and SMS integration): **$185**
* Toast Digital Storefront Essentials (this includes Online Ordering, Local by Toast, and Toast Delivery Service integrations): **$75**
* Kitchen Display Screen: **$35**
* DoorDash integration: **$30**

If you choose to run all of these integrations, you’ll pay $415 per month.

Now let’s add that to the cost of your actual Toast plan:

* **Starter Kit:** $415 per month (this plan is $0 a month)
* **Point of Sale:** $484 per month (this plan is $69 per month)

It’s a big investment, so knowing exactly what you’re paying for is important. Keep reaching because I’ll cover why I like Toast.

## **Where Toast stands out**

Despite the costs for various add-ons, Toast has a lot going for it, especially for restaurant owners. Here are some pros that I’ve noticed with Toast:

![Toast pros and cons](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/666eec3edcc552b5eecc7fcd/68265bdc73593ac6291ddf1f_toast-pros-and-cons-mobile%20(1).png)

* **Cloud-based:** The Toast suite is cloud-based and can operate offline if your internet goes out.
* **Accessible customer service:** Customer service is available 24/7/365, so there’s always someone to help if something goes wrong.
* **Customizable plan option:** With options like Build Your Own, you can tailor your plan to suit your unique needs.
* **Wide range of add-ons and integrations:** Features like Toast Mobile Order & Pay and digital storefronts make it easy to adapt to modern customer preferences. Keep in mind this is not an option for the Starter Kit.

### **What customers are saying**

Below are some examples of positive things customers had to say about Toast, according to [Trustpilot](https://www.trustpilot.com/review/toasttab.com):

**On reporting and customer service:** *“I love the reporting systems, the customer support has always been easy to reach on the rare occasion that we've had an issue and I feel as though the POS and software capabilities are truly top-notch for the price I pay each month.”*

**On offline usage:** *“We’ve had toast for almost 6 years now. It’s a great system. My most liked feature from Toast is the offline usage. My internet has gone out and we still function as usual.”*

**On add-ons and integrations: “***Menus are intuitive, swap over is super easy and their team is fantastic to work with. Also has fantastic integration partners, such as TipHaus. Let us pay our employees out the next day and automatically calculate tips for them.”*

## **Toast considerations**

While Toast has plenty of perks, it’s not a perfect fit for every restaurant. Here are a few things about the platform that I recommend keeping in mind:

* **Add-ons can get costly:** While the Starter Kit is free, add-ons and advanced plans can add up quickly, especially for smaller budgets. You’ll need to purchase Toast-specific hardware, which can be a big upfront expense and stretch your budget.
* **Doesn’t sync as well with other platforms:** Toast works best when you stick to its ecosystem, so relying heavily on other platforms may not be ideal. However, Owner.com’s [online ordering](https://www.owner.com/online-ordering) does pair well with Toast.
* **Requires Toast hardware:** You can’t use hardware that isn’t Toast-branded with the system. So, you’re pretty much locked into buying it even if you already have existing software.
* **Not as easy to use:** Reviewers have reported that their setup and onboarding are harder to set up than other platforms.

See what Toast users are saying below.

### **What customers are saying**

Here’s what customers are having trouble with when it comes to Toast, according to [Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/136301/Toast-POS/reviews/):

**On ease of use:** *“The initial installation required us to do a great deal of the set-up work, which required outside technical help.”*

**On** **costs:** *“It is significantly more expensive than what I was doing before and they forced me to buy all their hardware, like printers and tablets.”*

**On** **syncing with other platforms:** *“We tried integrating doordash into Toast and when we visited the shop on Toast it was locked and we were unable to add the integration.”*

## **Toast alternatives**

Toast can be great for a lot of things, but the perfect tool doesn’t exist. Some are better for [driving more online orders](https://www.owner.com/blog/how-to-increase-restaurant-sales) or for restaurants that have a retail store.

![Toast alternatives](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/666eec3edcc552b5eecc7fcd/68265c1ca33d1c9251ef8835_platforms-similar-to-toast-mobile.png)

Below are some [toast competitors](https://www.owner.com/blog/toast-competitors) I’d recommend considering for different goals:

### **Clover**

If you want a customizable POS system, [Clover](https://www.clover.com/pos-systems) could be a great choice for you. One thing I like about Clover is that it accepts more payment options than Toast. This can make things easier for both you and your customers.

| Category | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Best for | Customizable features and accessories |
| Free plan or free demo? | No |
| Pricing | Starts at 2.3% + 10¢ per transaction. Includes software fee of $14.95 a month |
| Overall rating | 3.2 |
| [Rating source](https://www.capterra.com/p/226864/Clover/), [Pricing source](https://www.clover.com/pricing) |

Clover is also designed to streamline in-store operations and staff management. Clover can handle employee schedules, track performance and make day-to-day tasks smoother.

Another big perk? Clover gives you way more flexibility with hardware. You can choose between a handheld device for tableside orders or a portable option for food trucks or pop-ups. It’s all about finding the right fit for how you run your restaurant.

If you want a POS that adapts to your business and gives you more control, Clover is definitely worth checking out.

### **Owner.com**

Owner.com is a [great alternative to Toast’s](https://www.owner.com/comparison/toast-vs-owner) online ordering features and complements a Toast POS setup in general. While Toast only offers basic online ordering as an add-on, Owner uses data to give you the best practices *automatically*. Our platform offers features like a robust [online ordering system](https://www.owner.com/blog/online-ordering-system-for-restaurants) designed to boost sales and drive direct customer engagement.

| Category | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Best for | Restaurants looking to boost online ordering efforts |
| Free plan or free demo? | Free demo |
| Pricing | Contact team for pricing |
| Overall rating | 4.7 |
| [Rating source](https://www.capterra.com/p/10002488/Owner/) |

What’s great about Owner is how well it integrates with platforms like Toast. If you’re already using Toast, Owner can:

* Push orders directly to your POS system
* Manage your menu seamlessly
* Sync updates automatically every six hours

Unlike Toast, Owner doesn’t stop at online ordering. We also offer:

* A [website builder](https://www.owner.com/blog/website-builders-for-restaurants) with advanced SEO features
* Automatic marketing with AI-powered menu pages and special offers
* Features that show customers how much they save by ordering directly through you

If your restaurant is established but looking to increase online sales, Owner.com is a great fit. It’s especially valuable when paired with Toast. This gives you the best of both worlds: robust POS functionality and advanced online ordering tools.

### **Square**

[Square](https://squareup.com/us/en/point-of-sale/restaurants) is a solid POS choice, especially if your restaurant also has a retail store. It’s budget-friendly, easy to use and comes with a free plan that’s perfect for new restaurants just starting.

What I love about Square is that it offers a ton of features, even in the free version. These include online ordering and team management tools. You also get helpful integrations for payment processing and menu management. Last but not least, you get a personalized mobile app to keep things running smoothly.

| Category | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Best for | Restaurants with a retail store |
| Free plan or free demo? | Free plan |
| Pricing | Plus plan starts at $29/mo. Premium plan is custom pricing |
| Overall rating | 4.7 |
| [Rating source](https://www.capterra.com/p/275800/Square-Online/), [Pricing source](https://squareup.com/us/en/pricing) |

If you’re ready to level up, the Plus plan starts at $29/month and adds more advanced features. For larger or multi-location restaurants, the Premium plan offers custom pricing and more features.

### **Support your growth with the right software**

Toast is robust [restaurant management software](https://www.owner.com/blog/restaurant-management-software) that offers a wide range of features to help you run your restaurant more easily. But it's important to understand Toast's pricing and requirements, as they may not fit every budget.

Plus, Toast is not the only option out there. If you're aiming to ramp up direct online ordering, give Owner.com a try. Take a [free demo](https://www.owner.com/demo) to see firsthand how we help restaurants grow their sales and thrive.

This article provides a detailed breakdown of Toast POS system pricing as of 2026, including upfront costs, monthly fees, hardware expenses, and integration add-ons. 

**Toast Pricing Plans:**
- **Starter Kit:** Free software, but requires upfront hardware and onboarding costs. Supports up to 2 terminals, one location.
- **Point of Sale:** $69/month software, more flexible, supports multiple locations, more add-on options.
- **Build Your Own:** Custom pricing based on selected features.

**Upfront Costs (One-Time):**
- Onboarding fees: $1,049 (includes $849 for 1-2 tablet setup, $100 for digital ordering, $100 for gift card conversion)
- Hardware costs: $2,645 (includes 14" Toast Flex with counter stand, Tap, printer, cash drawer at $1,049; kitchen display at $749; router $449; switch $59; kitchen printer $339)
- **Total upfront cost: $3,694**

**Monthly Recurring Costs:**
- Software recurring: $90/month
- Marketing Essentials (loyalty, gift cards, email/SMS): $185/month
- Digital Storefront Essentials (online ordering, delivery): $75/month
- Kitchen Display Screen: $35/month
- DoorDash integration: $30/month
- **Total add-ons: $415/month**
- **Starter Kit total with add-ons: $415/month**
- **Point of Sale total with add-ons: $484/month**

**Pros:** Cloud-based with offline mode, 24/7 support, customizable plans, wide range of integrations.
**Cons:** Expensive add-ons, requires Toast-specific hardware, poor syncing with non-Toast platforms, complex setup.
**Alternatives compared:** Clover (customizable, 2.3%+10¢/transaction, $14.95/mo), Owner.com (online ordering, integrates with Toast, 4.7 rating), Square (free plan, $29/mo Plus plan, 4.7 rating, best for restaurants with retail).

This webpage is a Toast hardware identification glossary and support resource, last updated July 31, 2026. It provides a comprehensive guide to identifying Toast hardware used in restaurant setups, including terminals, kitchen display systems, handhelds, printers, card readers, accessories, and network devices.

**Key hardware categories:**

- **Terminals**: Toast Flex 3 Terminal, Toast Flex 14", Elo Terminals (10", 15", 22" in V2/3 and V4 versions), Kiosk devices, and Terminals with Guest-Facing Displays (Toast Guest Display with Flex 3, Toast Flex for Guest, Elo Guest Facing Display - the latter is no longer sold but still supported).

- **Kitchen Display System (KDS)**: Toast Flex for Kitchen (14-inch) and Elo Kitchen Display Screen (various sizes), available on stands or wall-mounted.

- **Handhelds**: Toast Go® 1 (no longer sold but supported), Toast Go® 2 (built-in BBPOS card reader), and Toast Go® 3. Chargers and docks are not interchangeable between versions.

- **Printers**: Toast supports various printers identifiable by Toast or Epson logos.

- **Card Readers**: Toast Tap® for contactless payments. UK/Ireland/Canada models include AMS1, V400m, p400, S1 Handheld, and e285.

- **Accessories**: Zebra and Honeywell scanners, Brecknell 6710U Scale (only supported scale). Several older scanners are no longer sold but still supported.

- **Network Devices**: Toast Hub (ethernet switch), indoor/outdoor Wireless Access Points, Meraki Z3/MX64 Routers, and Toast Router.

Each device category includes links to installation guides, troubleshooting resources, and serial number location instructions.

**Pros:** Compact terminal. Works anywhere with 4G or WiFi. No ongoing fees. Simple to use. Holder or printer included. Works with or without POS.

**Cons:** Few on-screen features. Limited battery life without printer/charging dock.

**Buy if:** You want a stylish, pocket-sized card terminal for the till or on the go, with or without a receipt printer.

## How SumUp Solo works

SumUp is known for [its user-friendly, simple card payment solutions](https://www.mobiletransaction.org/sumup-review/ "SumUp review: affordable, no-fuss card readers with many extras") for small businesses and sole traders alike.

Its flagship model SumUp Solo is a special one: a square-shaped, standalone card reader without a physical PIN pad. Instead, it is operated exclusively via the front-facing touchscreen, like a purpose-built mobile device for card payments.

Photo: Emmanuel Charpentier (EC), Mobile Transaction

![SumUp Solo unboxing](https://www.mobiletransaction.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/sumup-solo-unboxing.jpg.webp "SumUp Solo box contents")

*All the box contents of a SumUp Solo package.*

The card reader comes with a built-in SIM card with unlimited data for 4G connectivity, but can also function through WiFi.

It’s therefore ideal as a mobile card terminal as well as for table-service in, for example, a small café with a secured WiFi network. It also connects with SumUp POS software for a complete, stationary till setup.

To accept a card payment without a POS integration, you enter an amount and custom description on the screen, proceed to add a tip (if relevant), process the card and print or send a digital receipt. Transactions can be viewed and refunded on the terminal.

Solo accepts a wide selection of chip and PIN and contactless cards and mobile wallets.

Payments settle in your bank account within 1-3 working days or the **next day at 7am (including weekends and Bank Holidays)** in an online SumUp Business Account linked with a complimentary Mastercard. If you like, you can then transfer funds to a bank account immediately.

You can order the Solo reader with a countertop stand or receipt printing dock that doubles as a power bank.

Photo: EC, Mobile Transaction

![SumUp Solo and Printer box](https://www.mobiletransaction.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/sumup-solo-printer-box.jpg.webp "The SumUp Solo and Printer package includes a receipt printer")

*For a higher price, you can get the SumUp Solo and Printer set.*

## Our opinion: unique terminal for a small business

SumUp Solo is an interesting card machine for payments that don’t require an integration with a POS system (though it does connect with SumUp POS). It works well for simple transactions where you just enter a payment total, not itemised receipts linked with a food menu or inventory library.

It’s fundamentally different from its predecessor [SumUp 3G](https://www.mobiletransaction.org/sumup-3g-and-printer-review/ "SumUp 3G and Printer review: lowest-cost terminal with receipt printer in UK") because of its touchscreen and compact design, but they are equally basic in their features.

If you want more advanced features, you may consider Solo Lite that connects with POS systems but doesn’t work on its own, or the mobile SumUp Terminal that contains some POS features.

| SumUp Solo criteria | Rating | Conclusion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Product** | 4.2 | Good |
| **Costs and fees** | 4.2 | Good |
| **Transparency and sign-up** | 4.8 | Excellent |
| **Value-added services** | 4 | Good |
| **Service and reviews** | 3.8 | Good |
| **Contract** | 5 | Excellent |
| **OVERALL SCORE** | 4.3 | Good/Excellent |

#### [How we rated SumUp Solo](#5ca1b94834c2fb751)

Mobile Transaction rates card machines – including SumUp Solo – in six different areas: product, pricing, transparency and sign-up, value-added features, reviews and support, and contract.

Each criterion gets a score ranging between 1 and 5, resulting in one overall star rating reflecting SumUp Solo’s value for a small business.

A card machine’s primary function is to take card payments in person, so the **device quality and experience of payment acceptance have a higher weighting** – this falls under the product criteria.

We thoroughly tested SumUp Solo and researched SumUp as a wider service to establish scores for the other rating categories.

With Solo, you can truly use it *solo*, anywhere with a mobile connection or wireless internet. The accompanying stand or receipt printer makes it great for, say, hairdressers and pop-up shops with a counter, and the tipping options are advantageous for hospitality and professional services.

**“I’d get the Solo with a printer, because the battery life can be short on its own, and the printer is a brilliant charger too. At a point of sale, though, you can just keep Solo plugged in.”**

– Emily Sorensen, Senior Editor, Mobile Transaction

Last but not least: the lack of monthly fees, commitment and complicated costs is attractive for a card reader. The upfront cost is low compared to traditional card machines, and the fixed rate competitive below a monthly turnover of £5,000.

*For alternatives, check out our [comparison of the best card machines](https://www.mobiletransaction.org/card-machine-small-business-uk/ "9 Best Card Machines for Small Businesses")*

## What are the card machine options?

SumUp sells two types of Solo card readers that are exactly the same size, but with crucial differences:

For a start, Solo Lite only works while Bluetooth-paired with an app on a mobile device connected to the internet. So the “Solo” before “Lite” is a bit misleading when it’s never truly functional solo.

However, Solo (without “Lite”) truly works on its own through WiFi or 4G or with a POS system when paired with a register.

Because Solo Lite is only switched on when a transaction created in SumUp app is ready for the card payment, the battery life of Solo Lite is much better than Solo at over 1000 transactions from a full charge. Transactions on Solo are created from start to finish via a power-consuming touchscreen, so it only lasts 100 transactions from a full charge.

#### SumUp Solo and Solo Lite compared:

|  | SumUp Solo | SumUp Solo Lite |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | SumUp Solo | SumUp Solo Lite |
|  | [Offer](/go/sumup-solo-uk/) | [Offer](/go/sumup-uk/) |
| **Price** | **£71** + VAT | **£22.50** + VAT |
| **Works without phone/tablet** |  |  |
| **Connectivity** | WiFi, 4G (SIM included) | Uses phone’s/tablet’s WiFi or mobile network |
| **Size** | 83 x 83 x 17 mm | 83 x 83 x 17 mm |
| **Battery life** | 100 transactions | 1000+ transactions |
| **POS integrations** | SumUp’s own POS system | SumUp’s own POS system |
| **Receipt printing** | Only via SumUp Solo counter or mobile printer | Connects with various Bluetooth printers |

![SumUp Solo](https://www.mobiletransaction.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/sumup-solo-300px.png.webp)
![SumUp Solo Lite](https://www.mobiletransaction.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/sumup-solo-lite-new-163x163.jpg.webp)

Solo Lite can connect with quite a few compatible, mobile receipt printers over Bluetooth. Solo has its own receipt printer (a stationary or mobile version) and does not work with other, generic-branded printers unless it’s through a POS system.

Photo: EC, Mobile Transaction

![SumUp card machine models next to each other: Terminal, Solo and Solo Lite](https://www.mobiletransaction.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/sumup-terminals-compared.jpg.webp "We’ve tested all of SumUp’s card machines to give an honest appraisal of them")

*SumUp Terminal is considerably longer than the Solo and Solo Lite terminals.*

### What about SumUp Terminal?

An alternative to Solo is SumUp Terminal. This is an oblong, traditional-looking card machine with a large touchscreen and built-in receipt printer. Like Solo, it works independently through 4G (SIM card included) and WiFi, so would suit table-side payments as well as mobile businesses.

It contains the same SumUp POS software as the app you download on a mobile device to use with Solo Lite. Yet Terminal’s ability to print receipts makes it more similar to the Solo + printer sets, as you can use them anywhere to accept cards and print receipts without an external device.

With a SumUp POS Plus subscription, Terminal even gets more features like open orders and preset discounts.

## Fees and pricing

SumUp Solo only costs a one-off price of £71 + VAT with just a desk stand or £98 + VAT with a receipt printer.

No setup fee applies, and it gets delivered for free within 2-3 working days. If you change your mind about the purchase, there’s a 30-day money-back guarantee on Solo.

There is no monthly fee, contractual commitment or other ongoing costs, just a fixed rate of 1.69% per card payment.

#### SumUp pricing:

|  | Charges |
| --- | --- |
| **Card machine price** | **SumUp Solo Lite:** £22.50 + VAT **SumUp Solo:** £71 + VAT **SumUp Solo + printer:** £98 + VAT **SumUp Terminal:** £121.50 + VAT  *Shipping is free* |
| **Contractual commitment** | None |
| **Monthly fees** | None |
| **Transaction fee (any card)** | 1.69% |
| **Payouts in 1-3 working days** | Free |
| **Refunds** | **Before payout:** Free **After payout:** Transaction fee is retained |
| **Chargebacks** | £10 each |

Payouts are processed free to your bank account within 1-3 working days or SumUp Business Account the next day.

It’s free to refund card transactions, as long as the transaction has not yet been settled in your bank account (i.e. within 1-3 days of the original transaction). After that, SumUp charges the original transaction fee for the refund.

If a customer disputes a payment, a chargeback fee of £10 occurs.

A membership subscription, Payments Plus, is available for £19 per month. This **reduces your chip and contactless rate to 0.99%** per transaction for domestic consumer cards (non-UK and commercial cards would cost 1.69%).

## The popular card machine: SumUp Solo

SumUp Solo is a totally unique card terminal to enter the UK market. It is the first card machine 100% designed by SumUp in-house by a team of over 100 engineers and product designers.

We know previous card readers – such as SumUp Air – were only partly designed by SumUp, using certain hardware components by third parties.

Photo: Emily Sorensen (ES), Mobile Transaction

![SumUp Solo checkout screen](https://www.mobiletransaction.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/sumup-solo-checkout-screen.jpg.webp "SumUp Solo checkout screen")

*SumUp Solo checkout screen.*

Photo: ES, Mobile Transaction

![](https://www.mobiletransaction.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/sumup-solo-menu-screen.jpg.webp "SumUp Solo menu screen")

*SumUp Solo menu screen.*

And the result? A simple touchscreen terminal that can constantly evolve with software updates.

I find it comfortable to hold in my hand, lightweight and easy to slide into a pocket. The built-in software is quite basic at this point, but SumUp may add features down the line.

| SumUp Solo tech specs | |
| --- | --- |
| **Dimensions** | 83 x 83 x 17 mm |
| **Card reader weight** | 147 g |
| **Display** | Touchscreen, greyscale |
| **PIN pad** | On touchscreen (no push-button PIN pad) |
| **Connections** | 4G, WiFi, Bluetooth |
| **SIM card & data** | Built in, unlimited free data |
| **Card reader technology** | EMV (chip), NFC (contactless) |
| **Battery life** | 100 transactions from full charge |
| **Accessories included** | SumUp Solo card reader, USB-C charging cable, charging cradle with clear lid, card brand decals |

### The screen

The (non-colour) touchscreen is highly responsive. When it’s on standby and not in the accompanying dock, you simply tap the dark screen to show the checkout screen.

Photo: ES, Mobile Transaction

![](https://www.mobiletransaction.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/sumup-solo-display-sunlight.jpg.webp "SumUp Solo display in sunlight")

*Solo’s display in strong sunlight.*

If stationed in the countertop- or receipt printer dock, you have to press the power button on the side to activate the screen.

You can adjust the screen brightness to suit any environment and set it to turn off the screen after 30 seconds, 1-5 minutes or never.

We tested the maximum screen brightness in strong sunlight, and the screen was still readable. It was grey and not bright in the sun, though better than its predecessor SumUp 3G’s display that had complaints about being hard to see in the sun.

### Battery life

The battery life is officially 100 transactions from a full charge, but in reality, it depends on how it’s used.

With maximum screen brightness and frequent testing, the battery on our Solo did not take more than an hour to use half its power. When we only used it for transactions with low screen brightness, it lasted longer.

Keeping Solo on standby drained the battery within hours when we first tested it, but SumUp has improved the battery life significantly since.

In addition, the **countertop and mobile receipt printer attachments act as a power bank** charging the terminal when low on battery (while placed in the printer). From a full charge, the mobile receipt printer can print up to 800 receipts without a recharge.

It takes a few hours to charge Solo from 0% to 100% in the basic desk dock, whereas the mobile receipt printer only takes 1 hour to fully charge itself and the card reader together.

### Software on Solo

What about the software? Here are the features:

**Checkout screen:** Numerical keypad where you enter a transaction amount and custom description to go on the receipt. You cannot enter multiple amounts for one bill or add products from an inventory library.

Photo: Mobile Transaction

![SumUp Solo transaction](https://www.mobiletransaction.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/sumup-solo-checkout-amount.jpg.webp "SumUp Solo transaction")

*You can only enter one amount per transaction.*

Photo: Mobile Transaction

![SumUp Solo custom description](https://www.mobiletransaction.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/sumup-solo-transaction-add-description.jpg.webp "SumUp Solo transaction description")

*Entering a transaction description can be fiddly with big fingers, as the keys are small.*

Photo: Mobile Transaction

![SumUp Solo loading screen](https://www.mobiletransaction.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/sumup-solo-transaction-wait-screen.jpg.webp "SumUp Solo loading screen")

*It can take several seconds before it’s ready to accept a card.*

Photo: Mobile Transaction

![](https://www.mobiletransaction.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/sumup-solo-tap-card-screen.jpg.webp "SumUp Solo tap card screen")

*Ready for a contactless or chip and PIN transaction.*

**Receipts:** After each transaction, you can send a receipt via email or text (all free). In a receipt printer, the terminal can of course print it too.

Photo: Mobile Transaction

![SumUp Solo send receipt](https://www.mobiletransaction.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/sumup-solo-send-receipt.jpg.webp "SumUp Solo receipt options")

*Receipt options after a payment.*

Photo: Mobile Transaction

![SumUp Solo text receipt](https://www.mobiletransaction.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/sumup-solo-send-sms.jpg.webp "SumUp Solo – send SMS receipt")

*Entering a mobile number for SMS receipt.*

**Tipping:** Enabling ‘Smart Tipping’ will display tipping suggestions before each payment, which usually increases your tipping income. The customer can either choose a tip like £2 or 15% (depending on transaction value), add a custom amount or choose not to tip.

Photo: Mobile Transaction

![SumUp Solo smart tipping](https://www.mobiletransaction.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/sumup-solo-smart-tipping-options.jpg.webp "SumUp Solo smart tipping options")

*Smart tipping options before a payment.*

Photo: Mobile Transaction

![SumUp Solo tipping settings](https://www.mobiletransaction.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/sumup-solo-tipping-settings.jpg.webp "SumUp Solo tipping settings")

*Tipping settings.*

**Connections:** Toggle on/off WiFi and log into your WiFi network from the main menu. If it’s off, the SIM card connects with the best available mobile network.

**Sales history:** Find past transactions on a date-ordered list. Tapping a transaction shows more details and options to refund or resend an SMS or email receipt.

Photo: Mobile Transaction

![SumUp Solo sales history](https://www.mobiletransaction.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/sumup-solo-sales-history.jpg.webp "SumUp Solo sales history")

*Sales history section.*

Photo: Mobile Transaction

![SumUp Solo transaction options](https://www.mobiletransaction.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/sumup-solo-transaction-options.jpg.webp "SumUp Solo transaction options")

*Transaction options.*

**Languages:** Set the terminal to almost any European language. This is useful for business trips abroad (SumUp allows usage abroad under some circumstances) or serving non-English-speaking clients.

That’s it for features.

### Updates and additional POS features

**You can connect the terminal with SumUp’s free POS app and SumUp POS Pro for complete till system features**. Solo is in fact the recommended card machine for SumUp’s hardware bundles for fixed counters, as it looks good and syncs well with the POS system.

SumUp may also decide to add new functions through its regular software updates. For instance, we experienced a sudden increase in language options from one day to another while testing.

The card machine automatically shows when new updates are available, but you can also check software updates manually on the terminal. If you need to, you can log out of the account from the settings menu (you must log in with your SumUp account details the first time you use it).

## Accessories and printed receipts

As a standalone card machine, you don’t have to connect Solo with anything else unless you want a full SumUp POS system.

If you buy the cheaper Solo package, the main accessory included is a non-slip display stand to put on a countertop. This doubles as a charging dock (not a power bank) with an internal storage compartment for a USB charging cable.

Photo: EC, Mobile Transaction

![SumUp Solo dock compartment](https://www.mobiletransaction.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/sumup-solo-stand-compartment.jpg.webp "SumUp Solo dock compartment")

*Solo stand’s compartment with USB charging cable.*

You can either plug the charging cable into Solo directly, or place Solo in the cradle and plug the cable into the dock to charge the card reader. You’ll need your own adapter plug for the USB cable, or charge it through a USB charging socket.

The countertop dock’s clear, magnetically attached lid is a great, stylish protection to keep the reader free from dust and dirt. The included decals showing all the cards accepted by SumUp Solo can be stuck onto the lid perfectly.

Photo: EC, Mobile Transaction

![](https://www.mobiletransaction.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/sumup-solo-stand-with-lid.jpg.webp "SumUp Solo stand with lid")

*SumUp Solo in its dock with lid on.*

Photo: EC, Mobile Transaction

![](https://www.mobiletransaction.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/sumup-solo-stand-chip-slot.jpg.webp "SumUp Solo stand chip slot")

*With the lid off, chip cards can be inserted.*

### Receipt printers

If you buy a Solo and Printer package, you don’t get the above countertop dock. Instead, you get a receipt printer-and-charging dock specifically designed for the SumUp Solo card reader.

There are actually [two versions of this](https://www.mobiletransaction.org/sumup-receipt-printers/ "SumUp receipt printers – what are your options?"): a stationary, square-shaped one and a mobile, curvy one. They cost the same in a bundle with the card reader (£98 + VAT), but if bought separately, the mobile one is pricier (£69 + VAT) than the stationary printer (£59 + VAT).

We have tested the mobile printer, which looks great as both a countertop stand and portable printer, so it works equally well at till point and on the go.

No other receipt printer works with Solo.

Photo: EC, Mobile Transaction

![SumUp Solo + Printer and SumUp Solo](https://www.mobiletransaction.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/sumup-solo-vs-solo-printer-compared.jpg.webp "SumUp Solo vs Solo and Printer compared")

*SumUp Solo in the mobile printer next to Solo in a basic desk stand.*

### Other POS hardware

You can connect the card reader with point of sale equipment like a cash drawer, barcode scanner and kitchen printer through the [SumUp POS Pro system](https://www.mobiletransaction.org/sumup-point-of-sale-review/ "SumUp Point of Sale (formerly Goodtill) review: affordable, not always smooth"). This is a customisable POS system for hospitality and retail, depending on your requirements.

Alternatively, it can connect with the SumUp app on a tablet, if you just need basic till features without a monthly cost.

Photo: EC, Mobile Transaction

![SumUp Solo and Printer underneath](https://www.mobiletransaction.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/sumup-solo-printer-underneath.jpg.webp "SumUp Solo Printer doesn’t store a charging cable inside")

*Underneath the SumUp Solo Printer, you have non-slip grips.*

Photo: EC, Mobile Transaction

![SumUp Solo next to printer](https://www.mobiletransaction.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/sumup-solo-next-to-printer.jpg.webp "SumUp Solo next to its printer")

*You can use the terminal inside or outside the receipt printer.*

## Reporting and other free extras

If you need more than a basic transactions overview on the terminal, you can log into your SumUp Dashboard on a laptop. Here, you can analyse sales and export sales reports.

You’ll also see many additional features (included free) such as invoicing, a product library and your SumUp Business Account.

Photo: Mobile Transaction

![SumUp web portal](https://www.mobiletransaction.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/sumup-dashboard-apr-2023.jpg.webp "Example of a SumUp Dashboard in April 2023")

*SumUp Dashboard in a web browser.*

**Even if you don’t have a card reader, we recommend downloading the SumUp app on your phone because it has lots of additional features.** You can send payment links, accept QR code payments, sell and accept gift cards, and create a basic online store.

The app also has an overview of payouts, employee accounts (staff can have different logins) and a product library to sell from.

## Customer service

All SumUp merchants can phone, email or message customer support on weekdays between 8am-7pm and weekends between 7am-5pm. Some customers do not get prompt support, while others do – calling is usually the fastest way to reach the team.

You cannot access help guides on the terminal, but it does show the URL to SumUp’s online FAQs that you can look up on your phone.

Photo: EC, Mobile Transaction

![SumUp Solo with MobileTransaction card inserted](https://www.mobiletransaction.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/sumup-solo-printer-mt-card-inserted.jpg.webp "Payment cards are inserted in the top chip card slot of SumUp Solo and Printer")

*SumUp Solo and Printer with a chip card inserted.*

## Getting started

SumUp is one of the easiest options around for getting started with card payments.

You simply [go on the website](/go/sumup-solo-uk/ "Get started with SumUp"), click to get started and complete an online sign-up form (takes about 5-10 minutes). You can then order the card reader online and wait 2-3 working days to receive it by post.

It may take a few days before your bank account – which must be in a name that matches your business name – is linked to your SumUp account, but you can still accept payments straight away. As soon as the bank account is verified, transactions can be released in your bank account.

Alternatively, you can choose to receive transactions in the online SumUp account, if you want to keep it separate from your bank account.

#### Emily Sorensen

# SumUp Solo Review Summary

## Overview
The SumUp Solo is a unique, square-shaped standalone card reader designed by SumUp for small businesses and sole traders. It features a front-facing touchscreen (no physical PIN pad), built-in 4G SIM with unlimited data, and WiFi connectivity. The device is operated exclusively via touchscreen and works independently or with SumUp POS software.

## Key Features & Specifications
- **Dimensions:** 83 x 83 x 17 mm, weight 147g
- **Display:** Greyscale touchscreen (readable in sunlight)
- **Connectivity:** 4G (built-in SIM with unlimited data), WiFi, Bluetooth
- **Battery life:** ~100 transactions per charge (Solo Lite offers 1000+)
- **Accepted payments:** Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Discover, JCB, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Samsung Pay, contactless
- **Transaction fee:** 1.69% flat rate (no monthly fees or contract)
- **Pricing:** £71 + VAT (with stand) or £98 + VAT (with receipt printer)

## Pros & Cons
**Pros:** Compact and portable, works anywhere with 4G/WiFi, no ongoing fees, simple to use, includes holder or printer, works with or without POS.
**Cons:** Few on-screen features, limited battery life without printer/charging dock.

## Comparison with Solo Lite
Solo Lite costs £22.50 + VAT but requires Bluetooth pairing with a mobile device and cannot work independently. Solo (standard) works fully standalone. Solo Lite has better battery life (1000+ transactions) since it only activates for payment processing.

## Accessories
- Countertop display stand (doubles as charging dock)
- Receipt printer (stationary or mobile version) that also acts as a power bank
- Clear protective lid with card brand decals

## Customer Service
Available weekdays 8am-7pm, weekends 7am-5pm via phone, email, or message. Phone is recommended for fastest response.

## Getting Started
Simple online sign-up (5-10 minutes), free delivery in 2-3 working days, 30-day money-back guarantee. No contractual commitment or setup fees. Payments settle in 1-3 working days (next day with SumUp Business Account).

Find the right payment tool for your business. Accept contactless, card and more on as many devices in as many locations as you need – all connected, all seamlessly integrated.

[LoadingShop card readers](https://store.sumup.com/en-us/product-selection/)

## Choose, connect, get paid

Set up the way that suits you – and manage all your payments in one place.

### Solo

A standalone, feature-rich card reader that grows with you as your business does.

## What will you pay?

One-time device cost

Monthly costs

In-person transaction fee

## The finer details

The devil’s in the detail, right? Have a look at the specs that might help you decide.

| SumUp Solo | Terminal |
| Hardware |
| Standalone device  Works independently without connecting a phone or tablet. | No | No |
| Portable  Allows you to take payments anywhere. | yes | yes |
| All-day battery life  Lasts an entire business day. | no | no |
| Touchscreen  Sleek touchscreen display instead of a traditional PIN pad. | no | no |
| Built-in receipt printer  Print paper receipts directly from the device. | Mobile or counter printer available | no |
| 1-year warranty  All hardware includes a 1-year warranty that covers any defects or issues. | yes | yes |
| 30-day money-back guarantee  Try it risk-free. If you’re not satisfied, return it for a full refund – no questions asked. | yes | yes |

## Still need help?

See what businesses like yours usually go for – and why – with our industry-specific recommendations.

[### Barber Shop](https://www.sumup.com/en-us/pos/barber-shop/?fcam_rc=406wrmsgwnul3c1ysuun9m05w)

## Ready. Set. Get paid.

Join the 4 million merchants worldwide who use SumUp to take payments. For better business, wherever it takes you.

[LoadingShop SumUp](https://store.sumup.com/en-us/product-selection/)

## Questions? We’ve got you covered.

### How do I set up and use my SumUp Card Reader?
:   Whether you’ve chosen the Plus, Plus Bundle, or Solo Card Reader, believe that using your SumUp Card Reader should be simple and intuitive. Check out the [**SumUp Help Center**](https://help.sumup.com/en-US/) to find step-by-step setup guides and helpful troubleshooting tips.

### Do I need an additional device to use my card reader?
:   The Solo Card Reader is a standalone device, so you don’t need to pair the reader with your smartphone or tablet in order to track or process your payments. The Plus Card Reader is the only reader that needs an additional device in order to accept payments. Learn more about using the Plus with your smart devices [**here**](https://www.sumup.com/en-us/plus-card-reader/)**.**

    If you’re using an iOS device, you’ll need to make sure it has Bluetooth 4.0 and its operating system is iOS 12 or higher. On an Android device, you’ll need Bluetooth 4.0 and its operating system must be Android 6.x or higher.

### How much do payments cost with a SumUp Card Reader?
:   All SumUp Card Readers are free from monthly and hardware costs. You only have to pay a standard 2.6% + 10¢ transaction fee whenever you take an in-person payment using your device.

### What cards do SumUp Card Readers accept?
:   All SumUp Card Readers and products accept major debit and credit cards, as well as NFC payment options. Choose from contactless, chip or swipe. You can find a full list of accepted cards here:

    * Visa
    * Mastercard
    * American Express
    * Discover
    * Diners Club
    * Google Pay
    * Apple Pay

### I’ve ordered my SumUp Card Reader. What happens now?
:   Once you’ve ordered your device, you’ll want to make sure you’ve completed your SumUp Account set up and business registration. Your device will arrive within 4-5 business days but won’t be able accept payments until your registration is complete and approved by our team.

\*30-day-money-back-guarantee from date of delivery.
